If Google Maps can help you find the quickest route home, Meowmbai can tell you where exactly to find the nearest cat.

The crowdsourced website, its name a play on “meow” and the Indian financial capital Mumbai, invites users to pin pictures of stray cats exactly where they are seen. The result is a familiar street map dotted with feline sightings across the city.

A quick glance at the map shows a ginger cat stretched across a compound wall in Bandra, another fast asleep on the seat of a bright orange motorbike in Colaba and a family of four on a sun-warmed pavement in Dadar. Hundreds more peer out from apartment complexes, tea stalls, and railway stations, each pictured by someone who decided that their neighbourhood cat deserved a place on the map.

It sounds like the kind of a niche idea that exists solely because one person thinks it’s fun, but its founder says the website is starting to have a real impact on the lives of so-called “community cats” – stray but familiar felines who go from house to house in a neighbourhood, relying on multiple regular feeders without having a single owner.

Sudarshan Birla, a 25-year-old product manager from Latur, a town about 500km east of Mumbai, had been living in the city for around a year when he was inspired to build the map by his frequent encounters with its many loveable strays. “I love documenting things,” Birla tells The Independent.

“Every time I took a picture of a cat, I felt it was attached to a place or memory. I would think, ‘This cat is from the corner near the tea stall that I walk past every other day.’ I wanted to build an interactive map where people could discover and revisit the city through them,” he says.

open image in gallery Meowmbai is a crowdsourced platform that invites users to pin photographs of community cats exactly where they are spotted ( Supplied )

The idea to build Meowmbai came together remarkably quickly.

Birla spent around two weeks building the website before launching it in June. While he expected fellow cat enthusiasts to enjoy browsing the map, he didn’t anticipate just how quickly people would begin adding their own sightings or requesting versions for other cities.

“I was severely overwhelmed by the kind of response that I received,” he says, but it also made him change the way he thought about the project. What began as a playful map of neighbourhood cats quickly attracted messages from community feeders, rescuers, and animal welfare groups, many of whom saw possibilities beyond simply cataloguing feline sightings.

open image in gallery What began as a playful map of neighbourhood cats quickly attracted messages from community feeders, rescuers, and animal welfare groups ( Supplied )

The more Birla listened to the people using Meowmbai, the more he realised that they weren't simply treating it as a novelty.

“Someone emailed me yesterday that they’d accidentally located the cat in the wrong location and wanted to update it,” he says. “This is something even I hadn’t thought about – that the user would actually think about these many details.”

Some users sought better ways to identify neighbourhood regulars, while others wondered if the map could eventually help reunite lost cats or connect injured animals with nearby rescuers.

The questions were surprisingly earnest for a website whose only real purpose, at least initially, was to answer one delightfully frivolous one: where are all the cats?

The answer, it turns out, depends very much on which city you ask.

open image in gallery Mumbai’s map rapidly became crowded with pins while India’s technology hub Bengaluru remained comparatively sparse ( Supplied )

When Birla expanded Meowmbai beyond Mumbai, he expected the map to fill up at roughly the same pace elsewhere.

Instead, each city began developing its own character. Mumbai’s map rapidly became crowded with pins, while India’s technology hub Bengaluru remained comparatively sparse, with only around 35 cats logged when Birla spoke to The Independent.

“Only Mumbai city has so many cats. You can spot a cat right away if you go out even for half an hour. But that might not be true for other cities,” he says.

“I was in Bengaluru for a short trip and went to Cubbon Park, one of the best places for a weekend walk. I saw so many dogs. There were Huskies, Labradors and Golden Retrievers. But I could only spot two or three cats.”

Whether Mumbai is India’s cat capital is impossible to say.

Unlike stray dogs, community cats aren’t routinely counted, and there is no official estimate of their population. But rescuers and feeders say Mumbai offers an unusually hospitable environment for free-roaming cats. The city’s dense residential neighbourhoods, fish markets, cafés, and restaurants provide a steady supply of food. In addition, generations of the city’s residents have quietly adopted local cats as unofficial neighbours.

open image in gallery Sudharshan Birla had been living in the city for around a year when he started the platform ( Supplied )

Even the municipal body has recognised their growing presence.

In 2019, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation became one of the first in India to approve a dedicated programme to sterilise community cats under its animal birth control scheme, despite acknowledging that no official feline census existed.

Though Meowmbai is not meant to function as a census of India’s cats, Birla is determined it should at least be an accurate record of the ones people encounter. Despite the growing number of submissions arriving each day, Birla manually reviews each photograph before it appears on the map, checking its metadata to verify the location.

As Meowmbai has evolved, Birla has become increasingly careful about the features. While some users have suggested highlighting neighbourhoods with large concentrations of cats, he has decided against it after conversations with rescuers and long-time caregivers.

open image in gallery Sudarshan Birla says Meowmbai started as a fun idea ( Supplied )

“One thing I’ve decided against is adding cat ‘hotspots,’” he says. “From the feedback I have received, if people see there are already lots of cats in an area, they sometimes abandon kittens there.”

“Meowmbai started as a fun idea, which I hoped people would really enjoy,” he says. “But it is now creating a real impact. That means I have the responsibility to build it thoughtfully. My immediate priority is to make sure that the platform creates genuine value.”

He hopes that, in time, it may become useful for rescue organisations, whether by helping spread information, supporting campaigns, or connecting people already working with stray cats.

But he insists he is still “in the learning phase” and wants to understand the needs of rescuers before introducing new features.

open image in gallery Sudarshan Birla he ‘would love to see people come to Mumbai and spend a weekend getting to know these cats’ ( Supplied )

For Birla, the biggest surprise has been not what the map has revealed about Mumbai’s cats but the people who have stopped to notice them.

“I already knew Mumbai had so many cats. But one thing I noticed was from the people's perspective,” he says. People he had never met offered suggestions and help and artists and animal lovers all wanted to contribute to something that, at its heart, was little more than a map of neighbourhood cats.

“I would love to see people come to Mumbai and spend a weekend getting to know these cats,” Birla says. “Maybe spend some time with them, feed them some good food, take a picture and upload it to Meowmbai.”

A South African couple found themselves in a rare situation when they witnessed a humpback whale “supergroup” consisting of nearly 300 of the giant marine mammals gathering together.

It's an indication, scientists say, of how some whale species numbers have strongly rebounded in the southern hemisphere oceans decades after an international whale hunting ban came into effect in 1986.

Chris and Monique Fallows said they were used to seeing bigger and bigger groups of humpback whales off the west coast of South Africa but weren't prepared for what they saw one morning last December. Plumes of whale breath and spray burst into the air one after the other from blowholes, and the husband and wife found their boat in the midst of what's known as a supergroup.

“It was extraordinary,” said Chris Fallows, a renowned fine art wildlife photographer who has documented marine animals for 35 years. "Quite quickly we realized that there must be several hundred whales coming together in one particular area.”

He said what they saw can best be described as a “Manhattan skyline” of whale breath plumes.

Chris and Monique documented 299 humpback whales in the group, they said. They count whales by taking a photograph of their tail, which is called a fluke, said Monique Fallows, an author and naturalist.

Each whale's tail is different and it's a common tactic used by scientists to identify individuals.

It appears to be the biggest group of humpback whales sighted, according to Alex Vogel, the Africa coordinator for Happywhale. That organization has a global database of whales built off photos and information sent in largely by what it calls “citizen scientists” — ordinary people who capture images of whales that are then verified.

The organization did a count of the group that the Fallows came across.

Humpback numbers have strongly recovered in the southern hemisphere from less than 10,000 at the height of whaling to more than 100,000 whales now, according to assessments by scientists and the International Whaling Commission, which monitors whale numbers.

Only a few countries still hunt whales commercially.

Humpbacks are generally solitary or move in small pods, but they sometimes gather in supergroups in food-rich areas. They feed on krill or small fish.

Sightings of humpbacks are also increasing in other parts of the Southern Hemisphere.

Els Vermeulen, the chief scientist at the University of Pretoria’s Whale Unit in South Africa, said humpback supergroups started to be seen again around 2012 and it's likely a result of their recovery from whaling.

“In general, the moratorium on whaling can be classified as one of the strongest conservation success stories in the marine environment," said Vermeulen, who has a doctorate in zoology.

Vermeulen said that humpbacks feeding in supergroups make underwater sounds that attract other whales.

While humpbacks have seen the biggest comeback from whaling, the World Wildlife Fund says the recovery has been mixed for other whale species and that various threats remain, like entanglement in commercial fishing equipment, collisions with ships and climate change.

Seven out of the 14 great whale species are classified as endangered or vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature, including the critically endangered North Atlantic right whales, which number only around 380 now.

Vermeulen also raised a new threat for whales around South Africa: the conflict in the Middle East.

She said a recent preliminary assessment she co-authored showed that shipping around the southern point of Africa had quadrupled since December 2023 — after the Israel-Hamas war broke out and Yemen's Houthi rebels began attacking ships in the Red Sea.

That is being made worse by the Iran war and the security crisis over the Strait of Hormuz, diverting more ships around Africa.

Because most whales killed by ships sink in the ocean there are no detailed statistics. But Gregg Oelofse, the coastal and environmental manager for the city of Cape Town, said more whales and more shipping clearly increase the risk.

He said some whale carcasses wash ashore with evidence they've been killed by vessels.

“We’ll see the propellor strike often through the whale’s body,” Oelofse said. “So, it’s like these big cuts in the whale’s body.”

Vermeulen said she and others are lobbying for official speed limits for ships near the South African coast to give them time to spot any whales in their path.

Associated Press writer Gerald Imray contributed to this story.

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.

News.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after settling for bronze
News.content:
Afterwards, Ramsay-Peaty, whose alleged dispute with his own family became a major distraction during his marriage earlier this year, was visibly emotional as he criticised the media which he insisted had written “rubbish” about his personal life.

“I know the s--- I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own, to be honest,” said Ramsay-Peaty, who lost his 100m breaststroke crown two years ago at the Paris Olympics. “But it does take a toll. The choices I’ve made over the last few months have been hard ones. But I’m happy at the same time that I can get here. I didn’t quit in Paris, but I deserve more.”

He added: “You don’t know who I am and people who comment, people who see the story because you read a headline, they’ve got to look themselves in the mirror,” Ramsay-Peaty told a group of reporters.

“You can’t hurt me. For me, it’s about my family and that does come at a cost. Being able to ignore that and being able to focus on my job – that hasn’t played a part in a sense of what we’re experiencing today.

“I’m still happy with that result. There’s some sense, but it has to, it has to stop. You know, look how many, how many athletes, how many people have to go for this until the media learn [a] lesson?”

Referencing Nowacki, the 18-year-old sensation from Jersey who has long been regarded as Ramsay-Peaty’s breaststroke successor, he added; “You have to learn and do better. You know, and for me, you know, I don’t want a young Filip one day to go through something like that, or these younger athletes.

“For me, that’s part of what I have to go through. I’ve got no control over that. But I think enough is enough. This is away from sport – it’s just about being decent people.”

After receiving his bronze medal, Ramsay-Peaty approached his wife, with whom he is expecting a child in December, and kissed her baby bump.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton hit with penalty in blow to Hungarian GP hopes
News.content:
Lewis Hamilton’s hopes of significantly denting Kimi Antonelli’s championship lead were dealt a blow after he was given a three-place grid penalty for Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

Hamilton looked to be the man to beat heading into qualifying at the Hungaroring and was on course for a record 10th pole position here before a messy final few minutes cost him.

Ferrari were well placed to end Mercedes’s run of having taken pole position for every grand prix this season. Instead, defending champion Lando Norris snuck in and took a superb pole for McLaren with a lap of 1min 17.207sec.

A poor final lap from Hamilton was compounded by a grid penalty for impeding the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, meaning the seven-time world champion will start fifth for the race at one of his most favoured circuits. The only consolation was that Antonelli was also given a three-place grid penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. The Italian will start seventh while Charles Leclerc, Hamilton’s team-mate, will be alongside Norris on the front row.

Heading into the final runs in Q3, Hamilton was 0.101sec ahead of Norris, but did not improve his time. Yet Norris, who was fastest in Q1 and Q2, and was the last of the top three across the line in Q3, had no problem, beating Hamilton’s time by 0.012sec.

Hamilton was critical of his Ferrari team for sending him out first, a decision he said “shocked” him.

“I don’t know why we went first, that was a bit of a shock to me and I definitely wouldn’t have chosen to go first,” Hamilton said. “I had a clean out-lap and when I started my lap and already in turn one I had a snap [of oversteer], I was already a tenth down. The last lap was the worst lap of all... we clearly had the car to be on pole.”

Worse was on the way for Hamilton. The stewards later confirmed the three-place grid penalty to add to the disappointment of missing out on pole.

Replays showed a frustrated Piastri gesturing to Hamilton for blocking him at turn one, ruining the Australian’s final flying lap. Hamilton said he was unaware that Piastri was there, which was proved by video evidence that showed how much he impeded the McLaren. It would have been an easy decision for the stewards to make.

News.title: ‘Always in bloom, a visit really makes one’s day’: Your favourite garden centres
News.content:
Bryan, 86, from the South East, has been a customer of Henry Street Garden Centre in Arborfield, Berkshire for decades: “My wife and I often used to browse and purchase plants and garden furniture.”

But his favourite memory was watching his wife’s “delight at their incredible Christmas displays of decorations. Lights, live reindeer even and the wonderful family atmosphere all around you,” he describes. “It’s still a magical place for me where I can get close to her memory.”

For Mary, 79, from the South East, “a garden centre is special if the plants are in season and healthy and there is great choice of both plants and compost”. She nominates family-run Grovewell Garden Centres at Swingfield near Folkestone, which has three other branches based in Kent.

Not only are their plants “always beautifully displayed”, she explains, they have “an amazing choice of garden supplies, cards and gifts, as well as a nice little coffee shop”. Her favourite memory, however, was at Christmas time a few years ago. “They have a couple of beautiful, nodding and interacting reindeer with a sofa in front of them. We were admiring them and an older guy on the staff asked if we wanted a photo taken, which was so sweet of him.”

“He took my husband’s phone and got a really happy little snap of us and the reindeer, which our girls thought was hilarious,” she says. “Service with a smile.”

Community spirit

News.title: Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe
News.content:
Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.

Kick-off is at 12.30pm.

News.title: How to choose a sports bra, with advice from a netball player, bra fitter and scientist
News.content:
How do you tell if a sports bra is the wrong size?

One of the biggest mistakes shoppers make is assuming that if a sports bra feels tight, that’s enough. In reality, support comes from the right fit rather than simply compressing your chest.

Cardwell advises thoroughly testing a sports bra by moving in it in the same way as you will during the sport you will be doing. “Your breasts don’t just move up and down,” she says. “They move all around – circles, up, down, left, right. We want to try and restrict that as much as possible, but not to the extreme where you’re not able to breathe.”

What is a high impact sports bra?

High-impact sports bras are designed for activities where your breasts experience the greatest movement, such as running, HIIT, tennis and netball. Their job is to minimise breast movement in every direction, helping reduce discomfort while allowing you to move more efficiently.

To measure how high-impact a sports bra is, Wakefield-Scurr asks women to run in a laboratory, both without a bra and while wearing different sports bras. “For a bra to be classed as high support, it has to reduce breast movement above certain thresholds,” she says. “If your breasts move 10 centimetres without a bra and five centimetres in a sports bra, that bra has reduced breast movement by 50 per cent.”

In the lab, Wakefield-Scurr and her team found that “if you run in low support compared with high support, you reduce your stride length by four centimetres. Four centimetres might not sound like a lot, but over the course of a marathon, those four centimetres add up to around a mile.” This proves that wearing a high-support bra doesn’t just keep you comfortable, but it can improve your athletic performance.

Cardwell, who wears a double G cup, says high-impact support has improved dramatically in recent years. “There has been a lot more research into high-impact sports bras, especially for larger-chested women.” She also warns against assuming that every sports bra offers the same level of support. “If it’s the same material as a smaller cup size, it’s probably not going to be sufficient for someone like me with double Gs.”

How often should you replace your sports bra?

There’s no set rule for replacing a sports bra, according to Wakefield-Scurr. This is because its lifespan depends more on how you care for it than how often you wear it. “The lifespan of a sports bra is affected more by how you wash and dry it than by how often you wear it,” she says. In one of her team’s studies, support dropped by around a third after 25 washes. “Always follow the washing instructions,” she advises. “You’d be surprised how many sports bras should be hand washed or washed at a lower temperature.”

Looking after your sports bra properly will help it last longer, but no bra lasts forever. Once the underband loses its elasticity or the support noticeably decreases, it’s time to replace it to ensure you have the right level of support.

Sports.title: England boss Thomas Tuchel takes in World Cup disappointment with London bike ride
Sports.content:
ENGLAND coach Thomas Tuchel gets a grip on his World Cup ­disappointment — by taking a ride on an electric hire bike.

The 52-year-old Three Lions boss looked in need of a pick-me-up as he went on a coffee run in ­Notting Hill, West London.



He bought himself a drink and handed another to a homeless woman.

A week earlier, he guided England to a 6-4 win over France to seal third place, our best World Cup finish since 1966.



But it came after an agonising 2-1 semi-final defeat to Argentina.

England had been leading until the 85th minute.

Tuchel came in for heavy criticism due to the substitutions he made while trying to protect England’s 1-0 lead.

The German coach then said England lacked the ‘DNA’ to control possession.



Midfielder Jude ­Bellingham, meanwhile, chilled at Disneyland, California, with his ­girlfriend Ashlyn Castro.

And his teammate Declan Rice was at Disney in Florida with his nephew.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick reunites with ex-boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in Norway before praising Man Utd’s academy stars
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK praised Manchester United’s academy gems for playing with swagger in the club’s 5-0 preseason win over Rosenborg.

Carrick again started with a strong side in Trondheim, but brought on two youngsters at the break in full backs Harry Amass and Jaydan Kamason.



Kamason produced two brilliantly worked assists, while Amass scored and played a fake one-two with Joshua Zirkzee to set up the Dutchman’s stunner.

Eight more youngsters arrived on the hour mark, with Jacob Devaney, on at centre-back, instantly finding the net before Ethan Williams completed the riot.



While it is still early days in pre-season, the most of the younger players have covered themselves in glory against Wrexham in Helsinki, and a limited Rosenborg side in Trondheim.

Carrick told MUTV in Norway: “That’s the best way to be as a footballer, when you’re in that zone and you’re confident, that’s my job to try and get the players in that frame of mind.

“The younger players, when you see them expressing themselves and being themselves and keep pushing themselves to be better.

“Some of the play in the second half was really, really good and I was delighted to see that from them.

“They’ve all got potential in different ways, and you want them to fulfil it and keep pushing themselves, and they certainly did that.”

Carrick met up with his former boss Ole Gunnar Solskjaer before the match on Friday.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The pair were both considered to take over from Ruben Amorim when the Portuguese was sacked in January.

Carrick did most of the coaching during Solskjaer’s three years in charge and that played a major part in the Geordie getting the nod over the Norwegian.

The pair have remained close friends and keep in touch, and Solskjaer’s family home in Kristiansund is a three hour drive from Trondheim.

Carrick worked under Solskjaer during United’s preseason friendly in Oslo against Kristiansund BK in July 2019.



Following the defeat to Wrexham in Finland and the more structured football in Norway, United head to Sweden next.

The Red Devils are back in action on Saturday when they face Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

Sports.title: New PM Andy Burnham actively considering letting football fans drink in stands again
Sports.content:
ANDY Burnham’s Government is actively considering letting football fans drink in the stands again.

Officials are considering whether to review restrictions which stop people consuming alcohol in view of the pitch.



The ban was introduced in 1985 to stop football hooligans fighting.

Other sports like rugby were not affected.



A government spokesperson said: “We are considering the case being made by some clubs and supporter groups for reviewing the current restrictions on alcohol consumption at football matches.

“The safety of football fans remains our priority, and any future consideration of changes would need to be evidence-led and informed by the views of policing and safety authorities, as well as clubs, supporters and other partners across the football sector.”



It comes just weeks after the new Prime Minister said it was “wrong” that spectators could not enjoy a pint during matches.

Everton fan Mr Burnham made the comments while watching a rugby league match at the club’s Hill Dickinson Stadium.



In a social media clip while holding a pint, he said: “How come these lads can do that in my seat here when we can’t do that at an Everton home game?

“There’s something wrong there, we need to take a look at that.”

This week the new Prime Minister announced that pubs, social clubs and live music venues will be given a 20 per cent cut to business rates from April.

Landlords welcomed the change but called on the Labour leader to go further by slashing VAT on boozers too.

The new Prime Minister insisted he was ready to protect “working-class culture” – in a win for The Sun’s Save Our Sups campaign.



More than 30,000 venues will save an estimated £1,100 each in the next financial year from the business rates cut.

Sports.title: ‘Sky’s the limit’ – Ayden Heaven talks up England hopes and could benefit from Man Utd mentor Harry Maguire’s misfortune
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED star Ayden Heaven insists “the sky is the limit” this season as he targets a dream England call-up.

And the Old Trafford teenager could be ready to carry the torch, just as mentor Harry Maguire’s proud Three Lions career likely enters its final chapter.



The 19-year-old centre half is targeting a major breakout year under Michael Carrick after waiting in the wings last term.

While Maguire has not retired from England duty, missing out on the 2026 World Cup squad at 33 suggests a natural transition is underway for the Three Lions—one Heaven has his eyes on.



When asked about pushing to be part of England’s Under-21s Euros title defence next summer, Heaven skipped a step to aim straight for the top.

He said: “I could push further than that. Maybe try and get into England, the main men’s team. The sky‘s the limit.



“I’ve just got to keep working hard every day. Harry has helped a lot, he has 20 years of experience.

“He’s always telling me to be vocal so I’m always ready when I get the opportunity to play.”

At this stage of his career, Heaven has only reached England Under-20 level.

He started 11 Premier League games last season, often when one of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt or Harry Maguire were unavailable through injury or suspensions.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Heaven said: “I’m young and I’ve got to be patient, especially in my position. You don’t see a lot of 19-year-olds playing week in, week out.

“I know it’s nothing personal and I’ve just got to be patient. I’m waiting for my opportunity.”

It’s almost certain Heaven will not be called up by Thomas Tuchel in the next September international break, but this season should be a banner with more games back in the schedule.

The teen is pushing to start alongside Maguire in United’s opening day clash against Hull City on August 22, having been the starting duo so far in pre-season.



With Lisandro Martinez forced off injured during the World Cup final and Matthijs de Ligt recovering from back surgery, the door has opened for the young centre-back.

Heaven’s main rival for a spot is Frenchman Leny Yoro, who is just a year older.

But with United’s World Cup stars still on break, Yoro has been deployed at right-back in their opening two pre-season friendlies against Wrexham and Rosenborg.

Heaven said: “We’re both young. We work hard every day in training together and we are close friends off the pitch.”

The Londoner earned high praise after filling the void left during crucial wins against Chelsea, Brentford, and Liverpool as United racked up three wins on the bounce to help secure Champions League football.



He added: “To hear the manager’s praise as an extra boost that he’s given up. He played a big part for this club when he played.”

Heaven, under contract until 2029, was former boss Ruben Amorim’s second signing, snapped up from Arsenal’s academy by Ineos for £1.25m.

Amorim liked Heaven’s game, but managed his minutes carefully, singling him out for applause after United’s 4-1 win over Wolves in December.

That came one match after he was substituted for Yoro at half-time after a challenging opening 45 minutes against West Ham.

Sports.title: Arsenal signing Christos Tzolis was tipped for the top from young age and almost poached by Barcelona at 12
Sports.content:
CHRISTOS TZOLIS has been tipped for the top by those in Greece since he was seven years old.

And the winger has finally reached the summit after Arsenal coughed up £34million to sign him on a five-year deal from Club Brugge.



The hefty fee has raised a few eyebrows given that Tzolis failed to make the grade during three nightmare years at Norwich.

But those at the 24-year-old’s first club, Greek side PAOK, are not surprised and can still remember when Barcelona tried to poach him at the age of 12.



Academy technical director at PAOK, Vasilis Mittas, told SunSport: “Christos joined us at the age of seven, with qualities that set him apart.

“From the very beginning, it was clear that he was an exceptionally talented footballer.

“Everyone who worked with Christos at the academy believed he had the potential to reach the very highest level and play for one of Europe’s biggest clubs.

“One memory that stands out goes back to our Under-12s team. As a reward for winning an international tournament, the club’s owner gave us the opportunity to play a friendly match against Barcelona at their training ground.

“We won 2-1, with Christos scoring one goal and providing an assist, playing a decisive role in the victory and producing the standout performance of the match.

“His display was so impressive that Barcelona expressed an interest in him immediately after the game.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Tzolis did not sign for Barca and nor did he let the hype go to his head, even after scoring 100 goals in a single season for one of PAOK’s youth sides.

Mittas remembers the winger as being “humble and grounded”, with those traits still part of his character today.

The Greek star had a month’s holiday this summer, but spent most of it training when he learned that Arsenal were interested in him.

Mittas said: “He never caused any problems off the pitch.



“He was the type of player who would do everything possible on the pitch to help his team succeed.

“Throughout his development at the academy, he played across all three attacking positions, but what truly distinguished him was his personality.

“He possessed an incredibly strong mentality and an unwavering desire to win.”

Tzolis’ mental strength proved vital when he left PAOK in 2021 as a 19-year-old and joined Norwich for £9m.

The winger failed to take off with the Canaries and spent two of his three seasons out on loan.



Tzolis bounced back, though, and rebuilt his career with 43 goals and 45 assists in 108 games over two seasons at Brugge.

Mittas added: “He has always been a fighter, someone who never gives up.

“Christos was still very young [at Norwich] and had to adapt to a completely new environment, a different culture, a new language and the unique demands of English football.



“What impressed me most was the way he responded. He never allowed that difficult period to define him.

“Everyone at PAOK believed he would come back stronger, and that’s exactly what he did.

“Looking back now, those challenges made him mentally tougher and played a significant role in shaping the player he has become today.”

Now 24 and coming into his prime, Mittas believes that everyone is starting to see the player PAOK knew Tzolis could be.

He has been signed by Arsenal to play off the left flank and replace Leandro Trossard, but can operate as a No10.



Tzolis models his game on Spain legend David Villa and his eye for goal has always been a big weapon.

Mittas said: “He has the instinct of a natural goalscorer.

“In every match, he finds a way to create or exploit one or two clear goal-scoring opportunities. He combines pace, explosiveness and excellent transitional play.

“I believe Christos is a perfect fit for Arsenal’s style of play, just as he is ideally suited to the demands of the Premier League.

“He is a player with significant room for further development, and I have no doubt that working every day under a coach like Mikel Arteta will help him reach an even higher level.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Ultimately, everything comes back to his character, work ethic and ambition. He always sets himself the highest standards and works relentlessly to achieve them.

“He is now entering what are traditionally considered the most productive years of a footballer’s career – and I firmly believe that his best football is still ahead of him.”

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes almost doubles annual income as Man Utd captain, 31, rakes in millions off pitch
Sports.content:
BRUNO FERNANDES scored a whopping £9.2MILLION in image rights payments.

The Manchester United skipper banked the huge sum in off-pitch earnings as he looks to agree a new deal at Old Trafford.



Fernandes, 31, is entering the final 12 months of his contract but club figures have told him they do not want him to leave under any circumstances.

United already have an option to extend the deal by a further 12 months — but they are hoping to increase it further.



Last season he became the first United player to win the Football Writers’ Player of the Year since Wayne Rooney 16 years ago.

Latest accounts filed by the Portuguese playmaker’s image rights firm show he tucked away £9.2m in off-pitch earnings.



And paperwork covering the 2024-25 season shows he has piled up £9.5m in BF8 Sports Ltd — the firm he set up in 2020 to use for off-field pay.

That figure shot up by £1.1m compared with the previous year — almost £100,000 a month.

After paying bills, Fernandes is left with £9,180,001.

And that is on top of his wages for playing.

Fernandes is reportedly on £12.5m a year at United, with bonuses, image rights and lucrative sponsorship deals with brands including Nike, DHL and EA Sports earning him more millions.

He is also reported to have a number of properties in both England and Portugal.

Fernandes is expected to join Man Utd’s pre-season campaign after completing his holiday following the World Cup where he represented Portugal.

Sports.title: Major update on Jack Grealish’s future as Enzo Maresca breaks silence on £100m England star frozen out under Guardiola
Sports.content:
IT was three years ago when Jack Grealish and Enzo Maresca were last together at Manchester City.

They were reunited at the Etihad Campus this week — but it looks highly unlikely it will last more than a few weeks.



Back in summer 2023 — when the Italian left his role as Pep Guardiola’s assistant to take charge of Leicester — Grealish, 30, looked to have the world at his feet.

He had just played a starring role in City’s historic Treble and was finally justifying his record-breaking £100million price-tag.



Yet, since then he has started only 17 Premier League games for the club and spent last season on loan at Everton.

Maresca, 46, revealed at his first press conference as the new boss on Friday the pair have stayed in regular contact. Like most people, the Italian clearly has a soft spot for Grealish.



Yet, when asked where it has all gone wrong for the former Aston Villa captain, Maresca said: “When you don’t work day by day with the players, it’s difficult to judge. I don’t know what he has done. It’s complicated.”

Grealish is still working on an individual programme as he battles back from the foot injury he suffered with the Toffees in January.

So he was unable to join in the sessions with the new boss at the City Football Academy but posted pictures on social media.

He wrote: “Nice to see everyone. I’m nearly there — hopefully not long now til I’m back training.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

No doubt it would have been nice to see Maresca, too. Although maybe he was hoping for a bit more encouragement from the new manager.

Instead the Italian said: “In any club I join, it’s my duty to coach the players at the club and Jack is here at the moment. I have a good relationship with him and since I left we’ve been keeping in touch.

“He has a big heart and is a very good guy but we’ll see what happens.”

It was hardly a ringing endorsement from an incoming manager — and the Three Lions favourite could be forgiven for seeing the writing on the wall.



So in a week when he was overtaken as City’s record transfer by another England man in £116m Elliot Anderson, Grealish finds himself at a crossroads.

Grealish was loved by both fans and staff during his loan spell down the M62 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium after he made such an encouraging start.

His season was ended by injury but he spent the final few months of the campaign working on his rehab on Merseyside — rather than returning to his parent club.

But, unsurprisingly given the way it all ended, the Toffees did not take up the £50m option to buy him permanently this summer.

Everton have not ruled out taking him back but another loan makes no sense for either him or City as he has just one year left on his contract.



David Moyes will want to see sure signs he is fully recovered before committing some of his transfer budget to signing a player who turns 31 in September.

His good pal and former Villa team-mate Gabby Agbonlahor believes Grealish’s days at City are over — and predicts he could even move abroad.

He said: “It will be interesting to see what happens with Jack, if he’s given a chance by Maresca. He would have been part of that City squad when Maresca was there as assistant.



“But will the manager think, ‘No’, and will Jack think, ‘Do you know what? Maybe I want to move on’?I don’t see him staying. Don’t rule out him going back to Everton.

“David Moyes loved him but it wouldn’t surprise me to see him play somewhere else in Europe.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

First, Grealish needs to get himself fit and Maresca must decide whether to give him one last chance at City, five years after he made his record-breaking move.

But time is running out for the Midlander — and plenty of people at the Etihad will feel he has had enough last chances.

Sports.title: Moment starstruck David Beckham hugs his basketball idol Michael Jordan on sun-soaked Ibiza holiday with their wives
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL legend David Beckham embraces his basketball idol Michael Jordan on holiday.

The sporting giants had lunch in sunny Ibiza along with their wives.



David, 51, wrapped an arm around fashion designer Victoria, 52, while Michael, 63, cosied up to Cuban model Yvette Prieto, 48.

At one point, former Manchester United and England star David, who is about 6ft tall, smiled as he looked up to 6ft 6in Michael.





When he left United for Real Madrid in 2003, David opted for the No 23 jersey – the same Michael wore for the Chicago Bulls.

He previously revealed he was starstruck after meeting Michael for the first time at a restaurant.

He recalled: “Even though he was sat at a table with Madonna and a couple of others, I was looking straight at him.”

“Victoria just nudged my leg and said, ‘Stop embarrassing me’.”



When Madge sent over champers, David and Vic went over to say hello.



He said: “Michael stood up and I shook his hand and his whole hand covered the whole of my arm.”

Sports.content:

Harry Kane was among the frontrunners for the Ballon d’Or following a stunning season with Bayern Munich but the England captain has been warned that he will be beaten to the award

View 2 Images Harry Kane England to the World Cup semi finals this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Harry Kane has been told that he is now out of running for the Ballon d’Or after England’s failure to win the World Cup. The Bayern Munich captain was among the favourites to claim the award after a stunning season in Germany.

‌



Kane, 32, scored 61 goals in 51 appearances in all competitions and helped Bayern to the Bundesliga crown, as well as the German Cup. But he was unable to lift his first Champions League crown, with the German side only managing to reach the semi finals.

‌



Meanwhile, Kane endured more heartache at the World Cup as England fell at the semi-final stage in the USA, the striker having scored six goals in seven appearances at the tournament.

‌



And former Arsenal and Chelsea star Emmanuel Petit has warned Kane that his failure to win either competition might have cost him his chances to win the Ballon d’Or.

Eddie Howe makes telling Bruno Guimaraes transfer admission as Arsenal prepare £70m bid READ MORE :

Speaking to Mr Gamble, the Frenchman said: "Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or chances are over. If you base that only on the German league, okay, no problem at all.

“But in the Champions League and with the national team, when it started to be really hard to win, I think he disappeared.

‌



“I can't point the finger at him because he tried everything he could, and he scored many goals, but he didn't have an impact in the big games, just like in the Champions League. So I think there are a few names ahead of him."

While Petit believes Kane is no longer among the contenders for the Ballon d’Or, he has suggested that there could be a few Spanish stars now firmly in the running after their success at the World Cup.

View 2 Images Kane scored six goals at the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

‌



He added: "Yamal? He had a great World Cup. You know the rules for the Ballon d'Or have changed so much, just like the rules on the pitch. Rodri has been the best player again during this competition. Messi had a great competition, but he plays for Miami."

"I know the World Cup is above any title you want with your club. But in the meantime, you have to win the title. Is it going to be a Spanish player? I have no idea. But it's going to be tough. And in the end, I hope it won't be a commercial decision."

Kane is currently on holiday after his international commitments but once he returns to Bayern Munich, he is expected to open talks over a new contract with the German giants.

Sports.title: Liverpool summer signing Jeremy Jacquet claims new team-mate is 'off his head'
Sports.content:
Liverpool summer signing Jeremy Jacquet claims new team-mate is 'off his head'

Jeremy Jacquet completed his move to Liverpool earlier this summer after a deal was agreed in January and it appears that his new teammates have already left an impression

View 2 Images Jeremy Jacquet agreed a deal to join Liverpool in January (Image: Getty Images)

Jeremy Jacquet has said that new Liverpool team-mate Jeremie Frimpong is ‘off his head’ after opening up on his move to Anfield. The defender officially completed his switch to Merseyside this summer, after the Reds agreed a deal for his services back in January.

‌



The 21-year-old could make his debut for his new club during their packed pre-season schedule. Having already been at Liverpool for a few weeks, Jacquet has discussed the welcome he received, as well as his new teammates.

‌



Speaking to Stan Sport, he said: "Yeah, so far that has all been going very well. They've given me a very warm welcome. And I'm getting to know them much better with every day."

‌



On the teammate he knows best, Jacquet added: "That depends… I'm trying to take the time to get to know everyone.

Liverpool receive huge Yan Diomande transfer update as £85m bid rejected READ MORE :

"But I spend a lot of time talking with Trey [Nyoni] and Leo [Giovanni Leoni], I often chat to Hugo [Ekitike] too of course. But other than these guys, I chat to everyone. A lot with Jeremie [Frimpong] too, who's off his head, by the way!"

Jacquet also saved a special mention for Liverpool supporters ahead of his debut campaign. He said: "Yes, I've had lots of messages from the fans, and I'd like to thank them for that. It's something that I really do appreciate, as I'd already received quite a few before I even arrived at the club."

‌



Jacquet could potentially make his debut for Liverpool on Saturday evening, with the Reds set to take on Premier League rivals Sunderland.

View 2 Images Jeremie Frimpong has made a big impression on Jeremy Jacquet (Image: Getty Images)

New boss Andoni Iraola has already spoken about the young defender and believes he is ready to make an instant impact at Anfield.

‌



Speaking last week, the Spaniard said: “Jeremy was a player that I knew very well, even before signing for Liverpool. Still being young, I think he has all the tools that we will need for that position.

“He also came into the last months of the [past] season with a shoulder injury, but he is fully healed. He has been already training with the U21s. He’s ready to go from the beginning.”

Following their clash with Sunderland, Liverpool have further games against Wrexham, Leeds, Monaco and Como. They will start their 2026/27 Premier League campaign against Eddie Howe’s Newcastle at St James’ Park.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino letter to Argentina 'leaked’ with astonishing claim on violent World Cup scenes
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino letter to Argentina 'leaked’ with astonishing claim on violent World Cup scenes

There are still ramifications unfolding from the chaotic World Cup final clash between Argentina and Spain in New York

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino's latest action may not go down too well amongst football fans (Image: Florencia Tan Jun, Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino wrote a swooning letter to the president of the Argentinian Football Association despite their violent reaction to losing the World Cup final. This letter has been leaked in Argentina, not long after FIFA opened an investigation into the violent fracas which followed Spain's 1-0 victory over the South Americans.

‌



The football world was left shocked as the likes of Leandro Parades, Nahuel Molina and even Argentinian assistant coach Roberto Ayala brawled with several Spanish players. FIFA issued a statement saying they were investigating "offensive behaviour and violations of the principles of fair play" in the Argentines.

‌



Despite this, Infantino wrote a letter to Claudio Tapia, president of the Argentina FA, swooning over the "professionalism" of the South Americans.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook pag

The letter read: "Dear Mr. President, Yesterday, Sunday, July 19, 2026, at the magnificent New York New Jersey Stadium, Argentina won the silver medal of the FIFA World Cup 2026, after an exciting final against Spain. I would like to reiterate my most sincere congratulations for this important new result for Argentine soccer.

"The FIFA World Cup 2026 will remain in memory as an unforgettable celebration of football, marked by spectacular matches, the irruption of new promises, the presence of the great figures of the sport and the extraordinary atmosphere lived in stadiums full of fans.

‌



"The magnificent performance of the Albiceleste also contributed decisively to making this edition an exceptional event that captivated millions of football enthusiasts around the world.

View 3 Images Infantino wrote to Claudio Tapia (right) (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista, Getty Images)

"Please send my sincere congratulations to all who have contributed to this magnificent result: to the players, to coach Lionel Scaloni, as well as to the coaching and medical staff and, of course, to the many fans who have accompanied and encouraged the team throughout the competition.

‌



"These victories are always the fruit of constant work, professionalism and attention to detail, but also of passion, commitment and love for this wonderful sport. All this augurs a very promising future and, without a doubt, will pave the way for new and great successes for Argentine football.

"I wish you, dear Mr. President, all the best for the next competitions and I hope to see you again very soon. With all my friendship, Gianni Infantino."

View 3 Images Infantino's letter will not chime well with football fans (Image: Justin Setterfield, Getty Images)

Article continues below

FIFA are yet to reach a verdict on whether Argentina's players will face sanctions over the post-match bust-up. In a statement released shortly after the final whistle, FIFA said: "Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with article 36 of the FIFA Disciplinary Code (FDC), the FIFA Disciplinary Committee has appointed a Disciplinary and Ethics Prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents.

"Further details will be communicated by the FIFA Disciplinary Committee once the prosecutor's report has been completed."

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford sent Michael Carrick message as Man Utd icons agree on transfer priority
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford sent Michael Carrick message as Man Utd icons agree on transfer priority

Marcus Rashford's future at Manchester United remains uncertain after Barcelona moved for both Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon this summer

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford (Image: (Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images))

Michael Carrick would love to have Marcus Rashford back in his Manchester United squad this season. That’s the view of Carrick's former Red Devils teammate Wes Brown, who also believes his old side also need to sign another centre-forward this summer - with Aston Villa's Ollie Watkins linked.

‌



Rashford's hopes of a return to Barcelona are all but over after the Catalan club announced the signing of Karim Adeyemi on Thursday. Adeyemi is Barcelona's second signing of the summer, after they bought Anthony Gordon for just under £70m from Newcastle United.

‌



The Red Devils, though, are keen to offload Rashford's £325,000-a-week wages, as that salary no longer fits within the wage structure at Old Trafford. However, Brown believes Carrick would jump at the chance to reintegrate him into the squad.

‌



"I'm sure Michael Carrick would love him back because it gives him another option," Brown told the Mirror. If he could come into the scene this season, that helps out massively.

"I'm still not sure what's going to happen, but I think if it was just up to Michael, he would definitely be back in. Obviously Marcus would have loved to have probably stayed at Barca. They went another way, so I'm not sure what other options there really are.

"For me, it’s always time. People always fall out and you can always rekindle things in football. It's just the way it is.

‌



Liverpool's Yan Diomande transfer hopes hit again as Real Madrid move for RB Leipzig star READ MORE :

"I think it'll be a boost for Michael for him to be here next season. He's on a lot of money, Marcus, so I think that's the only point that may make a move more difficult.

"He's a great player. His spells in the World Cup were showing it as well. It's a decision everyone's going to have to come to very soon."

United have already completed deals for Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans from Chelsea and Aston Villa for a combined £85million. But former Red Devils defender Brown, speaking via LiveFootballTickets, believes his old side needs to sign at least one more striker if they are to challenge for trophies again.

‌



"Obviously we needed to improve midfield," he said. "We've done that. We've done really well there. I think it's two great signings for the price as well.

View 3 Images Andrey Santos in action for Manchester United against Wrexham (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

"We've got one No.9 in [Benjamin] Sesko, [Matheus] Cunha can play there, but I think that area probably could be boosted. I think centre-half is fine, but I’m not sure about what happened to [Lisandro] Martinez in the final.

‌



"And then there's [Matthijs] De Ligt who hasn't featured [since November]. I would love another striker.

"I think when you're looking to win trophies, you probably need two or three that are all fighting for that place. I don't think we're quite there yet, but I do like the way we've done business."

Agreeing with Carrick, former United forward Louis Saha said: "I would love for them to sign an experienced striker who could help develop Benjamin Sesko.

‌



View 3 Images Benjamin Sesko and Matheus Cunha celebrate the former's goal for Manchester United against Liverpool (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire)

"He is a promising striker with incredible talent, so I would love to see him improve this season. I think signing a striker to guide and challenge him would be a smart move.

"United could also benefit from more defensive depth due to the increased number of games they will play this season.

‌



"I think signing cover at left-back and centre-back would be ideal so that they have flexibility in their squad and so when they rest players, the quality in the team doesn’t diminish."

Speaking via LiveFootballTickets, the Frenchman added: "I am concerned that the current Man United squad won’t be able to cope with the demands of next season.

"They are going to be in four competitions for the majority of the season, playing twice a week, which is a drastic change for these players compared to last season. It is also a big change for Michael Carrick, and it will be a real test of both he and his players' resolve next season."

Sports.title: Mason Mount opens up on new Man Utd role handed to him by Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Mason Mount opens up on new Man Utd role handed to him by Michael Carrick

Manchester United secured an emphatic 5-0 victory against Rosenborg in their second game of pre-season and Mason Mount has been left thrilled after being assigned a new job

View 2 Images Mason Mount ahead of Manchester United's friendly clash with Rosenborg (Image: Getty Images)

Mason Mount says he ‘loves’ being entrusted as a leader at Manchester United, having been handed the captain’s armband against Rosenborg. The midfielder was given the role by Michael Carrick against the Norwegian side in their second pre-season friendly after Harry Maguire was taken off.

‌



And it turned out to be a very productive outing for the Red Devils as they chalked up a 5-0 victory - Shea Lacey, Joshua Zirkzee, Justin Devaney, Harry Amass and Ethan Williams all finding the net.

‌



Mount was one of the most experienced players on the pitch throughout the evening and has said he is comfortable taking on more responsibility. He said: "You have different types of leaders.

‌



"You have ones that are very vocal, but I see myself as one who leads by example and never stops working. I've been captain previously, years ago, so I love the role.

Man Utd have Erik ten Hag to blame as another Marcus Rashford escape route blocked READ MORE :

"Especially with a lot of younger players on the pitch, and off it as well, being able to speak to them and make them feel comfortable, it's something I really like."

Another sight that United fans got to see against Rosenborg was a midfield duo of Mount and summer signing Andrey Santos. The Brazilian joined United in a £50m switch from Chelsea earlier this summer.

‌



"I've known Andrey for a while," Mount said about his new team-mate. "I've watched him from afar since he broke into the first-team at Chelsea.

View 2 Images Mason Mount was handed the captain's armband against Rosenborg (Image: Getty Images)

"He's a really good player and reads the game very well. He's a little bit more defensive, so it allows me to push on a little bit more and work off him.

‌



"Defensively as well, we're both players that want to get around it, put tackles in, win the ball back and be aggressive.

"I've really enjoyed it. It's a position I've played for many years from a young age. It's a position that I love, and I see myself in."

Mount, Santos and their Man United teammates will be back in action next week as the Red Devils continue their preparations for the new campaign. Their next assignment comes next weekend against Spanish giants Atletico Madrid before showdowns with Paris Saint-Germain, Leeds United and AC Milan. Carrick’s side commence their competitive campaign against newly-promoted Hull City away from home.

Sports.title: Man Utd given Manu Kone transfer deadline as Roma annoyed at slow deal
Sports.content:
Man Utd given Manu Kone transfer deadline as Roma annoyed at slow deal

Manu Kone is a man in demand this summer, but it appears his club have a deadline in mind to wrap up a transfer sale

View 3 Images Manu Kone is a man in demand this summer (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Roma are under pressure to sell Manchester United transfer target Manu Kone before July 31st. The Serie A side are at risk of a financial punishment from UEFA.

‌



They have a settlement agreement with the governing body of European football to ensure their losses do not exceed €60million (£51.25m) and have until July 31st to demonstrate this has not happened. Selling Kone, who is valued between £43m and £51m, would go some way to ensuring this does not happen.

‌



It's understood United have agreed personal terms, in principle, with the World Cup star, who was described as France's best midfielder by Patrick Vieira. However, a bid is yet to be sent by the Reds, despite their desire to sign a third midfielder.

‌



Corriere dello Sport, via Sport Witness, has reported that United have failed to progress in their pursuit of Kone, despite the agreement in principle reached with the 25-year-old.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Italian outlet also noted that United have been moving "slowly" in negotiations, much to Roma's annoyance. The Roman club are in a race against time, bound by their settlement agreement with UEFA.

‌



Offloading Kone would go a long way towards meeting that threshold and shielding the club from a fine of up to €10m, but it must be done 31st July, which is the deadline stipulated by UEFA.

Kone isn't the sole midfielder the Reds have been tracking. Real Madrid star and Kone's France colleague Aurelien Tchouameni continues to be touted for a switch to Old Trafford.

View 3 Images Kone was impressive at the World Cup (Image: Quality Sport Images, Getty Images)

‌



United have already strengthened their midfield options with the acquisitions of £35m Aston Villa star Youri Tielemans and Chelsea prospect Andrey Santos for £50m. However, with Casemiro having departed and Manuel Ugarte sidelined through injury, a fourth signing remains at the forefront of United's shopping list.

At the World Cup, Kone featured from the start in four of France's seven fixtures. During their semi-final loss to Spain, Didier Deschamps brought on Kone at the interval in place of Adrien Rabiot in a bid to spark a comeback.

Vieira has already endorsed Kone. Speaking in his punditry role, the 1998 World Cup winner, when quizzed about Kone, said: "He had a really good season in Serie A with Roma.

‌



View 3 Images Carrick is still looking to sign another midfielder (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

"He came to the World Cup after a couple of injuries. It has been quite a difficult season for him. He is for me today the best midfielder in France.

"I'd put him ahead of [Aurelien] Tchouameni and [Adrien] Rabiot, because he has this mobility, he is aggressive, he is a ball-winner, and he has the technical ability to be part of the build-up, has the facility with the ball to break lines and move forward."

Sports.title: Sheeraz escapes with narrow points win as he sets his sights on Canelo
Sports.content:
Hamzah Sheeraz escaped with a narrow points win, while Josh Kelly overcame a horror gash to his nose on the Anthony Joshua vs Kristian Prenga undercard in Saudi Arabia on Saturday.

Londoner Sheeraz, who sealed his first world title with a second-round stoppage win against Alem Begic to claim the vacant WBO super-middleweight crown in Egypt, defeated Germany's Simon Zachenhuber.

After a 12-round fight that ended with boos around the arena the judges returned scores of 114-114, 115-113 and 116-112, in favour of Sheeraz, who posed with Jacob Bank in the ring following his win.

"I am a champion in the division. I'm sure people are champing at the bit after [my] performance," said Sheeraz, who said he would be sat ringside on October 31 to watch Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez challenge for Christian Mbilli's WBC belt.

"I got the win, that's all that matters. I could make a million excuses. I'll be better in the next fight.

"I need a step up now, someone who will mentally present a challenge. I was switching off at times, I was too comfortable when I didn't have a threat in front of me."

Image: A bloodied Josh Kelly wins his IBF World Super Welterweight title contest against Caoimhin Agyarko

Josh Kelly overcame a horror gash to his nose as he secured a unanimous points win against Irishman Caoimhin Agyarko in an IBF Light-Middleweight title fight in Saudi Arabia.

Nicknamed 'Pretty Boy', Kelly was left bloodied as the pair clashed heads in the 11th round with the Brit's face left a mess.

But he did enough to get the win with scorecards of 115-112, 115-112, 114-113.

"I told Caoimhin, don't take it as a loss, take it as a learning. If he wants it bad enough, he will bounce back," said Kelly.

Agyarko said: "I thought I won it, but if it's not good enough for the judges, I accept that. I'm heartbroken, I wanted to make history. Josh Kelly is a class act, but I think he underestimated me a bit, there.

"Listen, it will come. I will be the first Black Irish world champion, there's no doubt about that."

After the bout, Kelly said he wants to face unified 154-pound champion Jaron 'Boots' Ennis.

Promoter Eddie Hearn, who represents both Kelly and Ennis, said a clash between the two in the States is now a real option.

"He's had a defence of the title and before that mandatory comes again, really you want to be looking at those big money fights and trying to roll the dice," Hearn said.

"I think that comes with 'Boots' Ennis. If I'm Josh Kelly I'm looking at the big payday out in America against 'Boots' Ennis. It's a three-belt unification fight. [WBC champion] Sebastian Fundora, all those guys."

Sports.title: In-form Leigh close in on top four of Super League
Sports.content:
In-form Leigh saw off Warrington 28-12 to close in on the top four in the Betfred Super League.

The Leopards, chasing a fifth straight win, made a fast start at Leigh Sports Village as David Armstrong stretched over in the corner and Lachlan Lam then finished off a sweeping counter-attack to touch down under the posts and give the home side a 10-0 lead after 15 minutes.

Adam Cook slotted over a 27th-minute penalty following an obstruction before the Wolves responded when Toafofoa Sipley powered through to reduce the deficit just after the half-hour.

Cook pulled another penalty attempt wide from the right, but Leigh then added a third try when Innes Senior was sent over in the corner down the left to take a 16-6 lead into the break.

Leigh saw Josh Charnley sent to the sin bin early in the second half following a high tackle on Toby King. Warrington then had Leon Hayes shown a yellow card in the 51st minute for a dangerous challenge on Owen Trout.

Joe Ofahengaue barged through to give Leigh a fourth try in the 53rd minute, with Cook kicking the extras and then landing another penalty to make it 24-6.

Umyla Hanley cut through the visiting defence to further extend the lead on the hour before winger Albert Hopoate got in down the right corner for Warrington's second try with 10 minutes left.

Leigh, though, saw out the closing stages, with Senior's late score in the corner chalked off for a forward pass, to continue their push towards the top four. They are now level on 26 points with Warrington, who have played a match less.

Leopards head coach Adrian Lam praised the way his side came through, despite having to make changes during the match because of injuries.

"I thought we were resilient today and hung in there and played really well," said Lam, who confirmed Frankie Halton suffered a suspected torn pectoral muscle which could rule him out for the rest of the season.

"The first half was awesome and we left some tries out there as well, but I though we were physical and we were up for it."

Warrington boss Sam Burgess felt his team deserved more.

"It is one of those games. I thought the scoreline probably didn't reflect the game or how tight the game was," Burgess said on Sky Sports.

"In that second half I thought we started with great spirit. We just couldn't get any points."

Lolohea inspires Giants to rare victory

The sides cancelled each other out in a tight opening at a blustery LNER Community Stadium, although Tom Inman thought he had given the Knights an eighth-minute lead after Cody Hunter's show and go and delayed pass, but a review showed he had grounded the ball short under pressure from George Flanagan.

However, they did go ahead within two minutes when Paul McShane's speculative kick was allowed to bounce in goal and David Nofoaluma pounced to touch down, Jon Bennison adding the conversion.

Mathieu Cozza passed up an opportunity to drag the Giants back into it with 20 minutes gone when he spilled the ball over the line, but winger Lewis Jagger's neat footwork and strength took him over within six minutes to reduce a deficit which Flanagan eradicated with the conversion.

Sports.title: Joshua devotes win to late friends as 'lovely treat' of Fury fight looms
Sports.content:
An emotional Anthony Joshua remembered his late friends as he staved off a seismic shock against Kristian Prenga to rubberstamp a fight with Tyson Fury that he says will be a "lovely treat" for fans.

Joshua knocked out Albanian heavyweight Prenga in the second round in Jeddah on Saturday night, after twice being floored himself in the first, including just 20 seconds into the contest.

The British star displayed tremendous character to battle back from the brink of defeat, a trait he has had to show in abundance since the deaths of team members Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele in a car crash in December in which he was a passenger.

Image: Joshua was sensationally knocked down by Albanian Prenga inside 20 seconds of their clash in Saudi Arabia

Speaking after overcoming Prenga, Joshua told DAZN: "It's more than punch power. That was spirit, that was Latz, that was Sina, that was the families. It hurts to even talk about it.

"It has been tough. It's my brothers. I don't want to talk about it."

Joshua: I respect everything Fury has done

Joshua was able to discuss Fury, with the British boxers now set to end over a decade of circling each other by locking horns in November, with America seemingly the most likely destination.

Fury beat Polish veteran Mariusz Wach in his own tune-up fight in Thailand on Friday.

AJ added of his countryman, who did hot head to Saudi Arabia for a face-off with his rival: "I am going to rip his heart out. I am the meanest and most vicious champion there has ever been!

Image: Joshua celebrates after his second-round KO of Prenga in Jeddah on Saturday night

"All jokes aside, I respect everything he has done and achieved but we are here now. I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat.

"I've learnt I can't be stopped. I won't be stopped and I won't be denied. We're here and we're coming. Trust me."

'No one can imagine what Joshua has been through'

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn confirmed that contracts have been signed for the blockbuster showdown before going on to praise his fighter's "astonishing" return to the ring after the "grief and pain" he had to deal with following the car crash shortly before Christmas.

Hearn said of Joshua on DAZN: "To be honest with you, tonight is all about the strength AJ has showed to even be here tonight - and the strength in that fight.

"No one can imagine what he has been through in the last seven months. During the first round, I was thinking, 'we came back too soon'.

Image: Joshua was floored twice in the opening round but bounced back to win and stay in course for a clash with Fury

"I feel boxing once saved him and I feel like he needed boxing to help him get through this. That camp allowed him to focus while he was facing so much grief and pain.

"He is a strong man and he likes to deal with his problems on his own - I'm not saying that is the right way but that is his way to do it. To even be in the ring tonight was astonishing.

"When you go down a couple ​of times in the first round and you're looking like ​your career might be over, he had to go to the depths one more time to get ‌up and fight on."

Sports.title: Joshua-Fury moves closer as AJ KOs Prenga after being knocked down twice
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua remains on course for a showdown with British heavyweight rival Tyson Fury later this year after recovering from being knocked down inside 20 seconds to secure a second-round knockout of Kristian Prenga in a wild clash in Jeddah.

Joshua endured a dismal first three minutes on Saturday night, hitting the canvas twice, firstly from a vicious uppercut, with the Albanian knockout specialist eyeing a seismic shock.

However, Prenga was demolished by right hands soon after in AJ's first outing since he was a passenger in a car crash in December that killed friends Sina Ghami and Latif 'Latz' Ayodele.

Image: Anthony Joshua was sensationally knocked down by Kristian Prenga in the opening 20 seconds

An emotional Joshua dedicated his win to his late team members, saying: "It's more than punch power. That was spirit, that was Latz, that was Sina, that was the families. It hurts to even talk about it. It has been tough. It's my brothers. I don't want to talk about it."

Fury had completed his own stoppage victory on Friday, over Polish veteran Mariusz Wach in a non-televised bout fought in front of a small crowd in Thailand, before vowing not to travel to Saudi Arabia for a face-off with Joshua, who he could now box in November.

There was no sign of Fury as Joshua overcame a boxer in Prenga who had recorded each of his 20 victories via knockout and won his previous 16 contests since a first career defeat in February 2017.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dev Sahni reveals how Tyson Fury toppled Mariusz Wach in a non-TV fight in Thailand

Prenga's stats made for strong reading and although there were no huge names on his CV he threatened a stunning result - one that could have shattered hopes of Joshua facing Fury - before the Brit registered his 30th win in 34 fights and second in a row, having beaten Jake Paul last year weeks before his car crash.

Fury contracts signed but no venue yet

After a hiccup-free weekend for Fury and Joshua coming through early adversity, a long-awaited all-British scrap looks set to happen in the autumn, with contracts already signed.

It could possibly be staged at 2am UK time at Wembley Stadium to suit a global audience but Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has said America is the preferred venue for fight organiser Turki Alalshikh.

If and when this clash does take place - Fury questioned whether Joshua would have the "guts" to challenge him as he spoke after dismissing Wach - boxing fans will get what they have wanted for years and, at various points, doubted they would ever see.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking ahead of the weekend, Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn hit back at Fury's claims he was worried about a potential bout against AJ falling through

Fears of Joshua suffering a fifth pro defeat, after two losses to Oleksandr Usyk - the same as Fury - and one each to Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz, were rampant after his shocking start against Prenga but his flurry of heavy blows in the second round earned him victory.

On Fury, Joshua added: "I am going to rip his heart out. I am the meanest and most vicious champion there has ever been!

"All jokes aside, I respect everything he has done and achieved but we are here now. I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat."

Image: Anthony Joshua walks to the ring ahead of his meeting with Kristian Prenga in Jeddah

Joshua also reserved praise for Prenga, saying: "He's a strong guy and I think Eddie [Hearn] wants to sign him now!

"He is going to do well and has a bright future. Maybe with a bit more experience, he will be up there with the rest of us.

"He is strong and durable and gave me a good test but this is what champions do, we rise. We get knocked down and stand up. That's life."
