World.title: Berlin: 1 dead, 16 injured after car ramming at CSD Pride event
World.content:
A citywide manhunt is underway after a van drove into a crowd during Pride celebrations, known locally as Christopher Street Day (CSD). Police have identified a suspect tied to Berlin's "Islamist scene."

What you need to know

1 person was killed and 3 people suffered life-threatening injuries after a car drove into a crowd at one of Europe's biggest LGBTQ+ Pride events

Police have identified a suspect associated with 'the Islamist scene in Berlin'

No arrests have been made, but a manhunt has been launched and more than 2,200 personnel have been deployed as part of the police operation

The area around the Tiergarten park in central Berlin has been closed off

At least one person has died and 16 people were injured, "some seriously", police said, after a vehicle was driven into a crowd near Berlin's annual Pride event, Christopher Street Day (CSD) on Saturday night.

"We believe that a vehicle entered the Tiergarten park and hit several people," police said on social media.

Berlin's CSD is one of Europe's biggest Pride events celebrating the LGBTQ+ community. It attracts tens of thousands of visitors from around the world each year.

What do we know about the incident at the Berlin CSD event?

Police spokesperson Florian Nath said a suspect has been identified who was known to police and "is believed to be associated with the Islamist scene in Berlin."

It was unclear whether there were other perpetrators. No arrests have been made yet.

Nath said a woman had died at the scene, without providing further details.

Three of the 16 injured had suffered "life-threatening injuries," Nath told reporters.

The city's fire department said eight people were seriously injured, with five sustaining minor injuries.

At least three of the victims suffered life-threatening injuries Image: Ralf Hirschberger/AFP

Nath added that more than 2,200 personnel were involved in the police response, including officers from Hamburg and other federal states.

The vehicle in question is a white minivan or compact SUV, he said.

DW reporters on the scene in Berlin said police officers armed with machine guns were patrolling the streets of the German capital.

The search for the perpetrators has been extended to the whole city Image: Christian Mang/REUTERS

Police said early on Sunday morning that the Tiergarten remained closed off.

"We are now piecing together the facts based on the evidence found at the scene. The search radius covers the entire city," Nath said. "We need to use daylight tomorrow to meticulously examine the evidence."

Berlin mayor, Chancellor Merz condemn 'horrific' act

Berlin Mayor Kai Wegner, who visited the scene, described the incident as "an attack on our free and open society."

"After a peaceful and colorful CSD, the assembly for a tolerant and peaceful Berlin was attacked in the most brutal way. Berlin is the city of freedom, and our freedom has been attacked in the most horrific way today," he said on X.

In remarks to reporters at the scene, Wegner said, "We will not allow our way of life and our way of living together to be taken from us."

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz also condemned what he called a "horrific act."

In a statement, Merz said he and Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt would ensure "this horrific act is fully investigated and punished."

'Today is a day of great mourning for the queer community,' Queer Berlin Liaison Officer Alfonso Pantisano said Image: Markus Schreiber/AP Photo/picture alliance

Pride parade participants told to 'go home, please'

Hundreds of thousands of people had taken to the streets of Berlin on Saturday to advocate for tolerance and diversity, culminating in concerts at the Brandenburg Gate.

The event was called off around 10:15 p.m., and a band's performance was interrupted. Authorities urged people to "go home, please," and avoid routes through Tiergarten.

Police told those attending a concert as part of the CSD event to leave the premises of the event immediately Image: Fabian Sommer/dpa/picture alliance

The CSD parade ended on 17 June Street, which crosses Berlin's Tiergarten to the Brandenburg Gate. The Gate has been the venue for concerts since Friday.

Berlin's CSD was first held in 1979, making it Germany's oldest Pride event. Its name comes from Christopher Street — the site of the 1969 Stonewall riots in New York City.

CSD has since evolved from a small protest into a major fixture of the city's cultural and political calendar.

Tens of thousands had celebrated Pride in central Berlin on Saturday Image: Fabian Sommer/dpa/picture alliance

Germany's history of car rammings

Germany has seen a number of car rammings at major public events in recent years.

In 2016, a Tunisian-born man drove a truck into a Christmas market in Berlin, killing 12 people, in the deadliest Islamist attack in Germany's postwar history.

In 2024, a man plowed his car into a busy Christmas market in the city of Magdeburg, killing at least two people and injuring more than 60. The perpetrator was a Saudi-born atheist who held anti-Islamic and far-right beliefs.

Earlier this year, two people were killed after a man drove a car through a crowd in the eastern German city of Leipzig. Investigators treated the incident as a rampage and the suspect, a German national, was remanded to a psychiatric hospital.

World.title: WAFCON 2026: What you need to know
World.content:
Several months after it was supposed to start and with more teams than first planned, WAFCON 2026 is finally set to begin. The hosts want a maiden title while a tournament outsider have one of its best players.

What is WAFCON?

The Women's Africa Cup of Nations is the continental tournament to find the best women's international team in Africa. It has existed in some form since 1991 but the current competition's history really starts in 1998; it has generally been held every two years since then.

Holders Nigeria have won a record 10 titles with only Equatorial Guinea (2012 as hosts) and South Africa (2022) having broken their domination of the tournament.

Originally planned as a 12-team tournament, the African football federation (CAF) added four more teams after qualification. Those four sides had all lost out in the second phase of qualifying but were then reinstated despite CAF earlier denying such changes were afoot. It was a sign of things to come.

Where and when is WAFCON 2026 being played?

For a third successive tournament, WAFCON is to be hosted by Morocco. Specifically, games are to be played in Rabat and Casablanca with a a third city, Fez, dropped from the initial lineup when the fixtures were announced.

Building the game from the ground up To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Since pulling out of hosting the men's AFCON in 2015, Morocco has become the favored African destination for both CAF and global football's governors FIFA. The North African country, which also hosted the men's AFCON last year, is to cohost the 2030 men's World Cup and has been chosen, or been the sole bidder, for a number of continental and international youth tournaments.

The tournament opener, between Algeria and Senegal, is on July 26, with Morocco opening against Kenya later that day. The final is scheduled for August 16 in Rabat.

Why is WAFCON being played straight after the men's World Cup?

It wasn't supposed to be. After weeks of rumor, denial and a South African offer to step in as hosts, CAF announced just 12 days before the tournament was due to start in March that it would be postponed. CAF, rather vaguely, cited "unforeseen circumstances" as the reason for the delay.

"It is a combination of factors, and it is not a decision taken lightly," Luxolo September, CAF's head of communications, told DW at the time.

"There is a question of the host nation, Morocco, requesting a postponement for a number of reasons. There has been a lot of interaction between Morocco, FIFA and CAF regarding the date. This is not a nice position for us. We have taken no joy from this. We would have loved to play in this window. It is a window we had requested."

Many teams, fans and players were frustrated by the short notice, with preparations made and money shelled out far in advance. It was not the first time though. Two years earlier, the tournament had been postponed by a year because the tournament clashed with the Olympics in Paris — a key date in the women's football calendar.

As well as coming hot on the heels of the men's World Cup, WAFCON 26 will now finish as the season starts in many countries. Germany's women's season for example, kicks off with the first round of the DFB Cup on same weekend as the WAFCON final.

Who are the favorites at WAFCON 26?

Hosts Morocco will want to match their men's side, who won their AFCON tournament in controversial circumstances earlier this year, their maiden title, having lost the previous two finals.

Nigeria wins women's Africa Football Cup of Nations To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Perennial champions Nigeria will once again enter as favorites while the 2022 winners, South Africa, will also fancy their chances. Below that are a host of teams who could cause a few surprises, including Ivory Coast, Egypt and debutants Cape Verde, whose men's side became one of the stories of the World Cup.

Who are the players to watch at WAFCON 26?

Apart from Zambia's Barbra Banda and Racheal Kundananji, Nigeria's Rasheedat Ajibade may be the most highly regarded talent. Named player of the tournament in 2024, Ajibade is a leader for her team, as well as its sharpest attacking threat. At the other end of the pitch, Nigeria will rely on Chiamaka Nnadozie, regarded as the continent's best goalkeeper.

Hosts Morocco will look to Ghizlaine Chebbak. The top scorer at the last two tournaments, 35-year-old Chebbak may not have too many better chances to win a first major international honor.

Elsewhere, Tabitha Chawinga, of French champions Lyon, will carry the hopes of debutants Malawi, the lowest FIFA-ranked side in the competition. Chawinga's international career has been interrupted by her club commitments but she has an exceptional 25 goals in her 11 caps to date. Her sister, Temwa, is also in the Malawi squad and plays her club football for the Kansas City Current of the NWSL, the top league in the United States. There, she won the 2025 Golden Boot as top goal scorer with 15 goals in 23 games.

Edited by: Chuck Penfold

World.title: Flavio Bolsonaro gets party nod to run against Brazil's Lula
World.content:
Flavio Bolsonaro won support from Argentine President Javier Milei and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, though tariffs imposed by Donald Trump's administration could complicate his path to the presidency.

Flavio Bolsonaro, son of Brazil's former President Jair Bolsonaro, was confirmed Saturday as his father's Liberal Party candidate to challenge incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

"Bolsonaro's blood flows here," he declared at the party convention in Sao Paulo.

His father has been sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup following his loss to Lula in the 2022 election.

Brazil's presidential election is scheduled to be held on October 4. If no candidate wins an outright majority, a runoff will take place on October 25.

Support from Milei and Netanyahu

The younger Bolsonaro still lacks a running mate and centrist backing, while the absence of major political figures at Saturday's party convention highlighted his struggle to build an anti-Lula alliance before October.

Bolsonaro (right) has received the backing of Argentinian President Javier Milei Image: Ettore Chiereguini/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

He did, however, get support from Argentine President Javier Milei, who endorsed his bid for the presidency.

"I firmly believe there is no one else capable of putting an end to the Lula risk hanging over Brazil," Milei, who attended the party convention, said.

Bolsonaro also showed a short video message of support from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Bolsonaro's campaign faces challenges

He has also developed ties with US conservatives and Donald Trump's administration. In May, he posted pictures he took in the Oval Office with the US president on social media.

The Trump administration has, however, since imposed new tariffs on Brazilian exports of up to 37.5%.

A poll released Friday shows Lula would defeat Flavio Bolsonaro in a potential runoff, 48% to 43%. A June survey showed Lula ahead 47% to 43%.

Lula's left-wing Workers' Party (PT) is expected to formally nominate him as its candidate in August.

World.title: Serbia's LGBTQ+ community faces 'epidemic of violence'
World.content:
Documented cases of violence against LGBTQ+ people in Serbia have never been higher. The attacks are part of a larger shift in society targeting marginalized people.

Amid a slew of blows and homophobic insults, the woman on the bus lashed out at Aleksandar Savic and stabbed him with a sharp object. Later, in the emergency room, doctors treated Savic for a cut to the calf and injuries to his eye.

Incidents like the July 11 attack on Savic — also know as drag queen Alexis Plastik — don't happen often in Belgrade. But violence against people who don't look or act like the mainstream in the EU candidate country is becoming increasingly common.

Just a few hours earlier, Vladimir Arsenijevic, author and program director of the annual Krokodil Literary Festival, was attacked in central Belgrade in the middle of the day by right-wing thugs, as he was preparing for a memorial event commemorating the 1995 Srebrenica genocide.

Speaking with broadcaster N1, Plastik called out the "epidemic of violence" in Serbia. The increasing violence by groups associated with President Aleksandar Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party, SNS, has reinforced the feeling among many people that anyone who is different can become a target, and that no one is safe.

Participants in the 2023 Pride parade in Belgrade were confronted by anti-gay protesters and a heavy police presence Image: Marko Drobnjakovic/AP Photo/picture alliance

"Violence is becoming increasingly normal, while protection against it is anything but guaranteed — especially for those who speak out against social or political problems, or who are unpopular with the general public," said Matija Stefanovic, the program coordinator for the LGBTQ+ group Da se Zna! ("For Your Information!"), which documents violence against queer people in Serbia.

"The fact that most of these attacks aren't investigated and that the perpetrators are rarely held accountable means they can't be dismissed as isolated incidents," said Stefanovic. "They represent a systemic problem that further stokes violence and emboldens perpetrators to continue attacking marginalized people, without having to fear significant consequences."

The social climate has become decidedly harsher for Serbia's LGBTQ+ community over the last few years, with the community also increasingly the target of right-wing nationalist government.

More recorded attacks than ever before

Da se Zna! is based in an unassuming office on a side street in the center of the Serbian capital. Aside from a lone rainbow-colored nutcracker standing on a shelf, hardly anything indicates the group's purpose: it's the only organization in Serbia to document attacks on queer people — threats, vandalism, physical assault.

Not much in the offices of Da se Zna! indicates the group's purpose Image: Tobias Zuttmann/DW

"Last year, we counted 110 cases — more than ever before," said Stefanovic. That's due in part to the fact that the NGO is becoming more well-known, and queer people are increasingly ready to report incidents. But dramatic, high-profile cases like the aggression against Alexis Plastik are also happening more and more.

In mid-May, unknown assailants attacked Mornar, a queer bar in Belgrade, with tear gas. At the end of May, a trans woman and her partner were beaten unconscious one night — again, by unidentified attackers.

Many queer people in Serbia are scared of openly showing their identity. In a recent survey by the European Union Agency for Fundamental Rights, some 80% of respondents said they avoided holding the hand of their partner in public.

The latest edition of the Rainbow Map , compiled by the International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association, shows that Serbia has slipped to 29th place in Europe, six spots below the European average. Five years ago, it was in 22nd place.

Support amid threats of violence

The only solution to this stigmatization and violence is education, said Stefanovic. Next to the yearly Pride parade co-organized by Da se Zna!, activists also travel to small towns around the country with a Pride Caravan to send a message: we're here, and we're not going anywhere.

In some of the towns, they're greeted by a handful of supporters holding rainbow flags — and dozens of demonstrators shouting homophobic slogans.

LGBTQ+ activist in Serbia: 'I was abused by the police' To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

After the group published a list of the planned destinations for this year's caravan, they received several death threats. The event in Pirot, in Serbia's southeast, was called off on short notice in mid-July because police could not guarantee the group's safety. Three journalists covering the event were attacked by the mob.

"These protests show the sad reality for queer people living in a small Serbian town," said Stefanovic. "We try to show the people living in these towns that we know how hard it is — and that we haven't forgotten about them."

Struggle to live openly in a small town

Stefanovic knows exactly how it feels to grow up queer in a small town far from the cosmopolitan city of Belgrade.

"I wanted to be a boy for as long as I can remember. Every night I prayed to God that he would turn me into one," he told DW.

Only when Stefanovic moved to Belgrade for his studies did he feel free to openly live as a man Image: Tobias Zuttmann/DW

Only as a teenager did Stefanovic learn about other people that felt like him — and that they were known as trans. But this knowledge did nothing to ease his worries.

"Once I realized [who I was,] I felt the weight of everything I would have to go through as a result," he said.

It was only when Stefanovic moved to Belgrade for his studies that he felt free enough to openly live as Matija. He came out as trans, first to several professors at the university, then to friends. Finally, one day, he wrote to his parents, an eight-page letter in which he explained everything that had preoccupied him for years.

Stefanovic then made two life-changing decisions: he began hormone treatment to align his biological sex with his gender identity — and he did so openly. At the time, there were very few people living openly as trans in Serbia, and not much information was available on how to undergo gender-affirming treatment.

"It sounds totally cliche, but I wanted to become the person that I needed in my life when I first exploring my own gender identify," said Stefanovic. He filmed his transition, first putting his videos on YouTube and then on TikTok.

TV interviews followed soon after — and the attention of right-wing groups on Facebook. At first, the hate directed toward Stefanovic seemed unbearable. But he decided to keep going, to stay visible, so that trans people would someday belong.

Stefanovic knows that acceptance is a process, and that people can change their views. His family is a prime example — his conservative father was the first person to consistently use the right pronoun and new name. And last year, both his parents took part in Belgrade's Pride parade for the first time.

"I'm so proud of them," said Stefanovic. "My parents have become my greatest allies."

World.title: Europe wildfires rage on, forcing more than 250,000 from homes
World.content:
From the outskirts of Bordeaux to communities near Madrid, fast-moving wildfires in France and Spain are driving mass evacuations, destroying homes, and claiming lives.

As wildfires continue to engulf massive stretches of western France and central Spain, more than 250,000 people have been forced to flee, with flames devouring forests and homes near Bordeaux and Madrid.

Firefighters have said that the blazes, the largest recorded in both countries in recent years, are so massive that they cannot be tackled head on.

Record wildfires in Spain, France force thousands to flee To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Man killed in wildfire near Valencia

The Spanish Interior Ministry said Saturday that a man was killed in a wildfire in the town of Manises, near Valencia.

Local authorities said firefighters managed to bring the blaze in Manises under control but "unfortunately the fire has claimed the life of one person." The body was found in a car in a ravine.

Two French firefighters died earlier this week near Bordeaux and one in Sicily, Italy, which is now also battling blazes.

Wildfires have forced the evacuation of some 250,000 people in southwestern France and central Spain Image: Violeta Santos Moura/REUTERS

On France's Atlantic coast, 44,000 people were removed from the Cap Ferret peninsula, many by boat.

Towns near Bordeaux, the famed winemaking town popular with tourists, were evacuated "as a precaution" as strong winds fueled approaching flames.

On Saturday morning, regional authorities further ordered the evacuation of three of the city's western suburbs "to ensure residents' safety."

In all, French authorities say more than 197,000 people have been evacuated in France's western Gironde and Landes departments.

In Spain, the Interior Ministry said 70,000 have been forced to flee.

Wildfires in southern Europe cause mass evacuations To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

EU sending firefighting aircraft to France and Spain

Authorities in France say the country's two main blazes were sparked accidentally, however, as summers become drier and hotter the magnitude of such fires has increased exponentially.

French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez, who said the government would do everything possible to protect citizens, warned that a wind shift had transformed the Cap Ferret blaze into "a large, self-sustaining fire that is extremely difficult to bring under control."

"It is now moving east, toward the Bordeaux metropolitan area," added Nunez, who pledged, "We are going to reorganize our response so we can fight it from the ground and prevent it from advancing toward Bordeaux."

Heat waves fuel wildfires across southern Europe To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

French President Emmanuel Macron called for European Union assistance on Friday as well as the mobilization of the French army to halt fires that have so far destroyed 22,000 hectares (54,000 acres) of land.

The European Commission announced that it is sending three firefighting aircraft to France and four to Spain in an effort to gain the upper hand.

This week's fires have injured dozens of firefighters and killed three of them — two in western France and one in Sicily, Italy, which is now also battling blazes.

The Tour de France has been shortened and will be effectively limited to Paris on Sunday because emergency services are needed to deal with wildfires in the country.

Spain declares national emergency

In Spain, the government has declared a national emergency as two of the country's three current fires, all burning near the capital Madrid, merge into one.

Madrid's regional emergency management services said the massive blaze has now reached "its peak and is currently beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain."

The largest active fire in the region, in Guadalajara province, has already laid waste to some 32,000 hectares.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez visited affected areas west of the capital on Saturday and stressed that the priority was "to save lives," as temperatures in the region topped 37 degrees Celsius (98.6 Fahrenheit).

NASA abandons comms facility amid Spain's summer of fire

The US space agency NASA on Saturday reported that it had been forced to evacuate its Madrid Deep Space Communications Complex (MDSCC), which is located in the region. The facility is one of three worldwide that allow the agency to communicate with spacecraft in distant parts of the galaxy — the others are located in Australia and the US.

"The safety and well being of our personnel is our highest priority and our thoughts are with the families and neighbors who are also experiencing the impact of the wildfires in the surrounding communities," said a statement released by the agency.

Wildfires raging near the Spanish capital Madrid forced the evacuation of a NASA deep space communications center Image: Gabri Solera/Europa Press/IMAGO

Spain, which regularly sees wildfires, has experienced an especially devastating summer. Earlier this month, fires in the south of the country killed 13 people.

Environmental officials say that 1,140 square kilometers (440 square miles) have already been lost to flames this year, more than five times the area burnt throughout the first half of 2025.

World.title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
World.content:
Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

For a healthy young woman in South Africa, the greatest risk of HIV may come from someone she wants to trust, but can't.

She may not know her partner's HIV status, may not always be able to insist they use a condom, and may have little control over whether he has other partners.

There is an option: Daily Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) pills keep antiretroviral drugs in the body at high enough levels to stop HIV before it can establish an infection.

But PrEP only works if she keeps taking the medication. Miss too many doses and drug levels can fall too low to provide sufficient protection.

She may forget, resent having to take a daily pill, or fear that a partner or relative will find the medication, causing stigma. She may also experience side effects from PrEP or struggle to obtain new supplies.

Zimbabwe takes a big shot toward an HIV-free future To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

How can lenacapavir help?

Taking medication consistently — known as adherence — is a challenge for people with conditions like hypertension and diabetes. With PrEP, however, the difficulty is even greater.

"You're asking people who are healthy, who don't have any illness, to take a tablet every day," said Salim Abdool Karim, director and co-founder of the Centre for the AIDS Programme of Research in South Africa. "That's a high bar."

"Repeated studies, including our own, show that patients who start taking PrEP, by month three, about half of them have given it up. By the end of the year, you're left with only a handful that are still taking PrEP," Abdool Karim told DW.

Lenacapavir sharply reduces that daily burden: It requires just one injection every six months.

"That's infinitely easier to do than to remember to take a tablet every day," he said. "For those who receive the injection every six months without fail, it works superbly because adherence is effectively complete."

But lenacapavir is still too expensive in some regions and access is low.

How does lenacapavir last so long in the body?

Most established PrEP drugs block enzymes that allow the virus to reproduce and spread — it uses the enzymes to copy its own genetic material and insert it into a human cell's DNA.

Lenacapavir works completely differently. It is the first PrEP drug to target the capsid, a cone-shaped shell that surrounds the viral genetic material. But the capsid is also essential to the virus' replication process, and therefore a promising target.

Lenacapavir attacks the capsid of HIV, shown in green because they are vital for the virus' ability to replicate and spread in the body Image: Cavallini James/BSIP/picture alliance

"[Lenacapavir] is the most potent molecule we know of against HIV," Wesley Sundquist, a University of Utah biochemist and leading expert on the HIV capsid, told DW.

Sundquist said lenacapavir remains effective over long periods and that it is potent even at low concentrations.

"It sets up a little depot that slowly dissolves," said Sundquist.

Which groups would benefit from lenacapavir?

Abdool Karim pointed to three groups where HIV incidence remains stubbornly high and greater PrEP uptake is urgently needed:

Adolescent girls and young women in parts of Africa

Younger gay men in the West

Vulnerable gay communities in Eastern Europe and Central Asia

In South Africa, a rollout for people at risk began in June 2026, backed by a July 2025 agreement between the drug's developer, Gilead, and a public-private financing organization called the Global Fund.

Gilead agreed to supply lenacapavir at no profit to up to 2 million people over three years.

Earlier, in October 2024, Gilead also agreed to allow the production of cheaper, generic versions of the drug in 120 resource-limited countries, where HIV infection rates are high.

But some countries still lack access to the drug.

Latin American countries excluded from lenacapavir deals

Melissa Scharwey of Doctors Without Borders said some Latin American countries, including Brazil, Mexico, Peru and Argentina have been excluded from recent rollouts of lenacapavir, despite having participated in clinical trials.

Even within eligible countries, vulnerable groups may still be missed, Scharwey told DW.

"There's by far not enough of it," said Scharwey, calling on Gilead to increase supply and sell directly to MSF at an affordable price of around $40 per shot.

The decisive question in driving down HIV, according to University of Washington epidemiologist Monisha Sharma, is whether the drug reaches the people and places where HIV is spreading most rapidly.

"In our modeling of South Africa, Zimbabwe, and western Kenya, providing lenacapavir to approximately 2–4% of the adult population, with targeted uptake among people at greatest risk, averted approximately 12–18% of new infections over ten years," Sharma told DW.

Is injectable HIV medication really a 'silver bullet'? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Lenacapavir 'unlikely to eliminate HIV on its own'

"Lenacapavir could substantially accelerate progress toward lowering incidence, but it is unlikely to eliminate HIV transmission on its own," said Sharma.

"This impact is highly dependent on affordable lenacapavir drug prices, efficient distribution channels, and targeted uptake among people with the highest HIV risk," she added.

That final condition is what gives Abdool Karim his greatest concern. Lenacapavir can largely solve the adherence problem for people who receive it. It cannot solve the harder problem confronting HIV specialists: identifying and reaching those in greatest danger.

"The problem is that those at highest risk need to come forward to take the medication. And often those at the highest risk don't see themselves at risk. That's why they're at risk," said Abdool Karim. "If we cannot reach those at highest risk, then we're not going to make a dent in this epidemic in the manner in which we were hoping."

Edited by: Zulfikar Abbany

World.title: Tour de France final stage shortened due to wildfires
World.content:
Security personnel assigned to the race have been redeployed to help contain major blazes near Bordeaux, reducing Sunday's final stage.

Sunday's final stage of the Tour de France will be shorter than planned because security forces have been redirected to help fight wildfires near Bordeaux, organizers and police said Saturday.

"In a spirit of national solidarity with the areas and communities affected, it was decided to adapt the route for the final stage from Thoiry to Paris," the Paris police and the event's organizers said in a joint statement.

Slovenian four-time champion Tadej Pogacar has all but sealed victory in the world-famous cycling race and only needs to finish Saturday's stage to secure a fifth Tour title in seven years.

Final stage shortened to 89 kilometers

The route for Stage 21 has been shortened to 89 kilometers (55 miles), down from the 133 kilometers originally planned.

It was set to begin east of Paris in Thoiry but will now start with two laps on the Champs-Elysees.

Riders will then race the circuit before finishing on the Champs-Elysees as usual.

The team presentation will still be held in Thoiry before riders are taken to Paris by bus.

The Tour first introduced the Montmartre loop to its final stage in 2025 [FILE: July 27, 2025] Image: Loic Venance/AFP/Getty Images

"The Paris police prefect and the Tour de France director salute the commitment of all the actors mobilized in the fight against the fires and express their full solidarity with the affected populations," the statement said.

Wildfires near Arcachon Bay, near Bordeaux in Gironde, and around Biscarrosse in Landes have destroyed more than 36,000 hectares of forest and forced nearly 200,000 people to evacuate.

World.title: Dozens dead after buses collide in eastern Syria
World.content:
The crash on a route notorious for deadly accidents prompted a large-scale rescue operation.

At least 35 people were killed and 30 others were injured when two buses collided in eastern Syria.

The crash happened on Saturday on a highway linking Damascus with Deir al-Zour province.

What else do we know about the crash?

The Interior Ministry said one bus was carrying security personnel, while the other was carrying civilians.

State television footage showed one of the vehicles engulfed in flames after the impact.

Military helicopters were dispatched to the site to help in medical evacuations Image: SANA/AFP

Military helicopters were sent to the scene to help evacuate the injured and recover the bodies.

The cause of the crash remains unknown.

The route is widely known as the "road of death" because of its frequent and often deadly accidents.

World.title: Los incendios de Madrid y Ávila afectan ya a 45.000 hectáreas y obligan a evacuar o confinar a más de 88.500 personas
World.content:
Las fuertes rachas de viento complican los trabajos de extinción de los fuegos, que no están controlados. La UME unifica el mando para coordinar la respuesta y el Gobierno amplía la emergencia nacional por los incendios a Toledo

Los incendios forestales que afectan ya a 45.000 hectáreas y han obligado a evacuar o confinar a más de 88.500 personas en la provincia de Ávila y la Comunidad de Madrid continúan activos y sin controlar. El viento complica por tercer día consecutivo las labores de extinción y la jornada del sábado fue difícil. El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, advertía de que la situación sigue siendo compleja: “No sabemos cuál va a ser la evolución del viento, pese a que las temperaturas hayan bajado”, señalaba por la mañana desde el puesto de mando avanzado en el municipio madrileño de Cenicientos (2.152 habitantes), que tuvo que desalojarse de urgencia por el avance de las llamas y se trasladó a la localidad vecina de Navalcarnero. La presidenta autonómica, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, calificó la situación como “totalmente inédita, nunca vista”. Palabras como “único” y “muy complicado” se repitieron durante todo el día.

“No ha sido un día positivo, no lo ha sido porque las condiciones meteorológicas han sido absolutamente difíciles, y si no ha ido a más, ha sido gracias al trabajo de todos los servidores [públicos]”, valoraba el ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, tras la última reunión del Cecop, sobre las 22.15. Las labores de extinción continuaron sin descanso con un objetivo claro: que las llamas del sur procedentes del incendio de Burgohondo, en Ávila, no confluyeran con las que avanzaban desde Madrid. El jefe de la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME), el teniente general Francisco Javier Marcos Izquierdo, añadió al balance del día que “los incendios no están controlados, pero la situación sí”.

Los frentes no se han unido, que era y sigue siendo el principal temor. La zona de separación es de unos 15 kilómetros, detalló Marcos desde el puesto de mando de Castilla y León, ubicado en Navaluenga. “Creemos que hemos detenido el avance de las llamas en el interior de esos dos incendios, así como en el flanco este que podía rolar hacia Madrid. El perímetro está definido, pero no está consolidado”, explicó ante los medios.

Aun así, los dos fuegos se tratan desde el sábado como un solo incendio para facilitar la coordinación. Y sobre las 19.15, el Gobierno anunció también que ampliaba la emergencia nacional por los incendios a Toledo, donde hay por el momento 11 municipios desalojados y no se descarta que haya más este domingo. “Nuestra prioridad está en salvar vidas y defender los núcleos poblacionales”, señaló Sánchez.

La secretaria general de Protección Civil y Emergencias, Virginia Barcones, también advirtió nada más comenzar la jornada de que el cambio de las condiciones meteorológicas iba a ser clave, como ya lo fue el viernes, y complicar mucho la evolución del fuego en Madrid. Las rachas de viento superaron los 50 kilómetros por hora, lo que obliga a adaptar la estrategia de extinción. La cabeza del incendio en Madrid se sitúa entre Robledo de Chavela y Fresnedillas de la Oliva, mientras que el fuego declarado en Ávila continúa moviéndose hacia el sur e inquieta su avance en el Valle del Tiétar, donde el Gobierno ha ordenado el desalojo de toda la zona. Allí se intensifican los trabajos de extinción.

Ante la virulencia y complejidad de los fuegos, el Gobierno declaró el jueves la emergencia nacional en ambas comunidades y desde entonces ha asumido el control de la situación. A media mañana, la UME informaba de que creaba un mando unificado para coordinar la respuesta entre Ávila y Madrid. Lo anunciaba el jefe de la unidad desde el puesto de mando: el operativo dejará de trabajar “como dos sectores independientes” para actuar “como uno único”. “Es la mejor forma de gestionar y ganar tiempo”, apuntó el teniente general.

Hace 48 horas, debido al rápido avance de las llamas, España solicitó a Bruselas la activación del mecanismo europeo de respuesta, que ha movilizado dos aviones desde Grecia y dos desde Italia, que llegaron este sábado a la península. También se desplazarán 100 efectivos del ejército de Portugal y 10 comunidades autónomas han enviado recursos para hacer frente a los incendios.

01:38 Ayuso: "Es un momento muy crítico"

Más evacuaciones en Ávila y Madrid

El incendio de Burgohondo, en Ávila, que ya afecta a 21.000 hectáreas según Interior, ha obligado a desalojar ya 16 municipios. En total son alrededor de 30.000 personas evacuadas y casi 8.000 confinadas en la provincia. La zona más conflictiva de fuego sigue estando en la zona sur, el Valle del Tiétar, según el delegado del Gobierno en Castilla y León, Nicanor Sen. Los vecinos recibieron durante todo el día las alertas en sus teléfonos móviles para que abandonen sus pueblos y se dirijan a las zonas preparadas para acogerlos. “Son desalojos preventivos”, explicaba Sen.

Los esfuerzos se centran en frenar el avance del fuego en esta zona y en evitar que se unan los dos grandes frentes. El teniente coronel de la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME) Pablo Samaniego explicaba que los incendios ya se están influyendo mutuamente debido a las condiciones meteorológicas, aunque todavía no se han unido físicamente: “Trabajamos para que esa unión física no se produzca”. Ya hay una persona detenida y otra investigada como responsable del incendio forestal en Ávila. Según la Guardia Civil, ambas habrían utilizado maquinaria pesada en una zona donde estaba prohibido su uso, lo que provocó una chispa que originó el fuego.

En Madrid, los tres fuegos activos en un principio terminaron fusionándose en un solo gran frente que arrasa desde hace ya tres días la esquina suroeste de la región y afecta a 24.000 hectáreas. “Es el peor incendio de la historia de la Comunidad de Madrid”, lo calificó la presidenta autonómica. El delegado del Gobierno en la región, Francisco Martín, habla de “un incendio único”. En la comunidad hay ya 12 municipios evacuados y cuatro confinados. En total son 29.488 las personas que duermen fuera de sus casas y 21.132 los confinados en sus pueblos.

Por el momento, solo se conocen los daños materiales en una de las primeras urbanizaciones que tuvieron que ser desalojadas en Madrid. Fue en la localidad de Encinar del Alberche, donde 43 casas han quedado destruidas y 286 dañadas. Es el primer y único balance provisional de destrozos causados por los fuegos, pero ofrece una imagen preliminar de lo que se irá conociendo a medida que avance el fuego.

World.title: Última hora de los incendios forestales, en directo | El Gobierno amplía la emergencia nacional por los incendios a Toledo
World.content:
El Summa ha atendido a 80 personas desde el inicio del incendio en Madrid

El Summa 112 ha atendido a 80 pacientes desde el inicio del incendio en la Comunidad de Madrid, según ha informado este sábado el Ejecutivo regional en un comunicado. De las 80 personas, 65 recibieron el alta en el lugar y 15 fueron trasladadas a hospitales de la red pública, todas con pronóstico leve.

Entre las seis de la tarde del viernes y las ocho de la mañana de este sábado, los equipos de emergencias asistieron a otros 18 afectados, entre ellos un bebé y varios bomberos, sin que ninguno presentara lesiones de gravedad. A la asistencia prestada por los Soportes Vitales Avanzados y Básicos se añaden las decenas de intervenciones realizadas por la Unidad de Psicología de Emergencias del Summa 112, que coordinará el refuerzo de profesionales que comienza este sábado gracias a la colaboración del Colegio Oficial de la Psicología de Madrid, en contacto permanente con los psicólogos de la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME).

El SUMMA 112 mantiene desplegado un dispositivo integrado por una decena de recursos de Soporte Vital Avanzado y Básico, además de las Unidades de Apoyo Logístico, Apoyo Sanitario, Coordinación de Catástrofes y Mandos Operativos. También dispone de ambulancias de Transporte Sanitario No Urgente destinadas a las evacuaciones de residencias y centros sociales cuando se ordena el desalojo de un municipio. Asimismo, el servicio forma parte del Puesto de Mando Avanzado (PMA), que esta mañana ha sido trasladado de Cenicientos a Navalcarnero.

World.title: Los Gómez contra las llamas: “La Guardia Civil nos quería detener por cortar unos árboles para que el fuego no llegara al restaurante”
World.content:
Los pinchos morunos, la chistorra y los chorizos, restos de una barbacoa frustrada, descansan sobre la mesa junto a una botella de aceite retorcida por el calor. Solo dos tiendas de campaña se han librado del fuego en el camping del valle de Iruelas (Ávila), donde dos toallas tendidas, semiquemadas, ilustran el milagro. Lo demás está arrasado. Huele a plástico quemado, los muchísimos bungalows se han prácticamente derretido, una moto es ahora un amasijo metálico, y de la cama elástica solo queda el esqueleto. Así parcela tras parcela por el azote del fuego de Burgohondo, devastador en el sur abulense. Los bosques han ardido, y con ellos el entorno de casas y negocios para desesperación de muchas familias que temen el golpe económico que viene.

Es el caso de los Gómez, hosteleros de la zona, conscientes de que las llamas han abrasado su economía. Ya lo van intuyendo pese a que se mantienen ocupados: faltan manos contra el fuego. Los tatuajes de Karen Gómez, de 28 años, señalan el camino. “Resiliencia”. “Coraje y corazón”. La fina tinta negra tiñe su piel como lo hace la ceniza en los bosques donde se criaron y disfrutaron tantas como ella. Ahora los árboles son tótems humeantes. “La culpa es del descontrol de siempre”, reniega el sábado por la mañana, 72 horas después de las primeras chispas, cuando afirma que no había medios. Luego, pese al útil embalse cercano, faltaron los cruciales helicópteros.

El infierno estalló el jueves. Desalojos, miedo, huidas. Erick, de 30, explica con los ojos rojos de no dormir y faenar entre el humo que un grupo de vecinos y visitantes de La Rinconada, una aldea entre la arboleda y el pantano, se quedaron atrapados. Le tocó meter a seis en una barca, entre ellos dos guardias civiles que fueron a analizar la situación, y sacarlos por el agua, donde los caballos se sumergían para alejarse del frente. No le importó que hace un tiempo perdió un dedo y parte de los músculos del brazo en un accidente en esa misma barca.

“Es surrealista que alguien de Madrid que no ha pisado el campo haga leyes rurales”, censura, agradecido a las brigadas forestales donde actuó varios años y crítico con la Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME), a la que acusa de inacción. El patriarca, Jesús, de 56, toma café con evidentes cortes en los brazos de la pelea nocturna. “La Guardia Civil nos quería detener por cortar unos árboles para que no llegara el fuego al restaurante”, afea, delante de ese negocio donde trabaja, ahora vacío. “¡Póngame los grilletes!”, respondió.

Los tres enseñan vídeos del otro hermano, Nick, de 23, toda la noche apagando incendios con cuadrillas voluntarias cerca de Val de San Martín, otro punto crítico. Ninguno de los cuatro ha dormido y aun así se activan rumbo a las viviendas de Rinconada, muchas chamuscadas, una de ellas directamente hundida por el fuego, con los cristales destrozados. Los chavales suben a una pick-up, llevan una motosierra junto a su amigo José María Guerrero, de 47, habitante allí y tenso todas estas jornadas. “¿Con esa navaja lo vas a cortar?”, bromea, por fin ligeramente distendido, tras tantas horas de drama. Pues sí. Erick ejerce sus conocimientos forestales y corta el tronco de un metro de diámetro y 20 de largo que ha caído sobre el camino que conduce hacia otra localidad. Entre todos empujamos la madera para conseguir retirarla. Allí se quedan los tres.

Una casa quemada en La Rinconada, en el municipio de El Barraco (Ávila). Emilio Fraile

El padre se ha quedado sin vehículo y pide a los periodistas que lo lleven a El Barraco, también víctima de las llamas estos días, donde su pareja regenta un hostal. Por el camino, entre más humo y llamaradas repentinas y un señor guiando a dos caballos, uno de los cuales presenta llagas en una pata, el hombre cuenta su historia con el fuego.

-Este es mi tercer incendio.

-El peor, ¿no?

-No. El primero me arruinó la vida. Tenía una empresa de pinturas en Madrid y ardió todo. El seguro no cubrió nada. Luego puse un restaurante y se me quemó también.

Al menos ahora el negocio de su pareja y el bar donde trabaja él han resistido. Le llaman preguntándole por distintos inmuebles y responde a su interlocutora que su terreno se ha salvado. “Qué alegría me has dado. Te quiero mucho, Jesús”, se escucha al otro lado del teléfono. El encuentro con su esposa, María José Hernández, se produce en el hostal El Encuentro, donde está durmiendo también una cuadrilla de bomberos venida desde Segovia. La mujer se derrumba: “Está siendo demasiado duro, un horror”. Hernández presume de familia, con hijos y sobrinos comprometidos con su Ávila, fajándose ante la percibida como ausencia de fuerza institucional, sin el respaldo que precisan. “¡Se estaba quemando todo y no había nadie!”, evoca sobre el maldito miércoles donde tardaron horas, según sus recuerdos, en aparecer los medios. La abulense prevé que el incendio, que ha devastado “un paraíso”, va a comprometer a múltiples familias que viven del paisaje, de su paz, de su descanso: “La gente tiene que venir. Si no, ¿de qué vivimos?”.

Erick Gómez trabaja para retirar uno de los troncos caídos sobre los caminos de La Rinconada (Ávila). Emilio Fraile

La conversación trascurre con cierta calma hasta que por las ventanas se divisa una nueva columna de humo negro. Salir a escape conduce a una urbanización cercana al embalse, con casas desperdigadas, casi entre el bosque y rodeadas de matorral: una amenaza tremenda. Los vecinos se despliegan y colaboran con los bomberos de distintas procedencias alistados en la batalla contra el fuego. Se tienden mangueras, se sacuden los batefuegos, se grita contra la humareda y se exclama con alegría cuando por fin llueve: es el agua que cae de los helicópteros, maná entre la sequía de sonrisas.

World.title: Hallado un hombre muerto en el incendio de un barranco de Manises (Valencia)
World.content:
El audio de esta noticia utiliza una voz sintética generada por Inteligencia Artificial y podría tener algunas inconsistencias.

Cinco personas han sido trasladadas al hospital por inhalación de humo y quemaduras como consecuencia del fuego, ya estabilizado

Un hombre ha fallecido este sábado en el incendio declarado en el barranco del Salt de l’Aigua en la localidad valenciana de Manises. El Ayuntamiento de la localidad ha confirmado la muerte en un mensaje en las redes sociales: “Lamentablemente, el incendio se ha cobrado la vida de 1 persona. El Ayuntamiento de Manises decreta dos días de luto oficial, mañana y lunes”.

Según varias informaciones, el fallecido, una persona de avanzada edad, había ido por la mañana a su huerto junto al barranco, cuando le ha sorprendido el fuego. Los profesionales de la extinción del fuego han hallado el cadáver de la víctima, que podría haber inhalado humo y no habría podido ponerse a salvo. También ha aparecido su coche calcinado.

El incendio ha arrasado sobre todo matorral y ha generado una intensa humareda visible desde Valencia (a 14 kilómetros). Se ha dado por estabilizado por la tarde.

Cinco personas han sido trasladadas al hospital por inhalación de humo y quemaduras como consecuencia del fuego, según ha informado el Centro de Información y Coordinación de Urgencias (CICU). Tres han recibido ya el alta y dos permanecen en observación, según las mismas fuentes.

Dos medios aéreos y nueve dotaciones de bomberos han trabajado para sofocar este fuego, declarado sobre las 12:45 horas en un área de vegetación del barranco del Salt de l’Aigua de Manises (Valencia), según el Consorcio Provincial de Bomberos de Valencia.

Al lugar del fuego se han desplazado seis dotaciones de bomberos, dos BRIFO, un sargento, un coordinador forestal y un oficial del Consorcio. Además, ha acudido también una unidad de bomberos forestales y dos medios aéreos de la Generalitat. En total, al lugar del fuego se han trasladado tres ambulancias de Soporte Vital Básico (SVB) y otras dos de Transporte Urgente, según el CICU.

World.title: ¿Cuántas hectáreas han ardido? El mapa de los incendios activos más graves
World.content:
En las últimas dos semanas se han iniciado en España {{fires_2weeks}} incendios, {{bigfires_2weeks}} de ellos han sido grandes incendios forestales de más de 500 hectáreas. Eso indican los datos provisionales del Sistema de información europeo de incendios forestales (EFFIS) que miden la extensión de los fuegos a partir de imágenes satelitales.

En el siguiente mapa mostramos dos cosas: los polígonos que actualiza EFFIS y otros estimados por EL PAÍS a partir de los puntos de calor que detectan los satélites. Usamos estos puntos para clasificar los incendios: cuando hay puntos de las últimas 24 horas sobre un incendio o sus inmediaciones se ven en rojo ( activo 24 horas ); cuando son de las últimas 48, pasan a naranja ( 48 horas ). Así, un incendio con polígono rojo y muchos puntos rojos será activo y reciente.

Cargando En el mapa se muestran los incendios activos en las últimas 48 horas y los puntos de calor recogidos por distintos satélites: 24 h 48 h. Más incendios graves Desde mayo Cargando incendios activos...

La información de puntos de calor activos la recopilan cinco satélites de la NASA que detectan focos de temperaturas anómalas mediante sensores térmicos. Para determinar el perímetro del incendio usamos los datos del programa europeo EFFIS, basado en fotografías satelitales: mide el área quemada casi tiempo real, por lo que ofrece cifras provisionales y sirve para seguir la temporada al día. Sus números suelen ser algo más altos que los del Ministerio de Transición Ecológica, que ofrece la estadística oficial más precisa a partir de los partes de incendio de las comunidades autónomas, pero con semanas o meses de retraso. Ambos deben tomarse como una estimación que se consolidará al final de la temporada.

En el mapa también puede consultar las zonas de riesgo de incendios en el territorio. Este {{date_aemet}} habría peligro extremo de incendio en {{area_riesgo_extremo}}% de la superficie peninsular, según las estimaciones de Aemet.

¿Cómo está siendo la temporada?

Según los últimos datos actualizados de EFFIS, en España se han quemado {{area_ha_year}} hectáreas desde el principio de año hasta este {{today}}, por encima de la media de los últimos 20 años a estas altura de la temporada.

Ha despuntado también el número de incendios, que se sitúa ya en {{fires_year}} –sobre la media de {{fires_mean}}–, con un incremento del {{fires_summer_inc}}% desde el inicio del verano.

¿Qué está pasando en Europa?

En el conjunto de la Unión Europea, la superficie quemada asciende a {{ue_area_year}} hectareas, {{ue_aera_over_mean}} por encima de la media.

World.title: Cuando “evacuación” es la palabra del día: niños, vecinos discapacitados, perros y también autoridades
World.content:
El incendio que recorre Madrid a toda velocidad parece tener conciencia propia. Hace unas horas se dividía en tres frentes que ahora, tras atraerse y fundirse en un todo por la dinámica de las corrientes de aire, forman una sola lengua de fuego que arrasa allá por donde pasa. Y, como si tuviera claro a dónde apuntar, se acercó con mala intención a la base de su principal enemigo: el Puesto de Mando Avanzado (PAM) desde donde las autoridades diseñan la estrategia para combatirlo.

El PAM estuvo instalado hasta este sábado a las afueras de Cenicientos, junto al cementerio y el tanatorio municipal. Desde esa loma en la que están enterrados los antepasados de los vecinos de este pueblo de la sierra de Madrid se veían con claridad las llamas que devoran el monte. Era el lugar perfecto para dirigir el despliegue de miles de efectivos sobre el terreno. Sin embargo, el fuego llegó a estar demasiado cerca, lo que convirtió en un peligro permanecer ahí. En ese momento el cielo se había vuelto naranja y una espesa niebla envolvía todo.

El desmantelamiento del PAM se ha interpretado como lo que es, el reflejo de que la situación es muy grave. La noticia cogió por sorpresa a todos. La presidenta Isabel Díaz Ayuso hablaba con la prensa cuando el delegado del Gobierno, Francisco Martín, la interrumpió y se puso al frente del micrófono. “Vamos a proceder a evacuar el municipio de Cenicientos, por lo que vamos a desmontar este PMA. Les rogamos que vayan saliendo de aquí de manera ordenada y con calma”, dijo. En cuestión de una hora todo quedó recogido.

En Cenicientos y los alrededores sospechaban que iba a ocurrirles lo mismo que a los otros 12 municipios de Madrid que han sido evacuados. Forman parte ya de los 29.488 desalojados por un incendio que ya ha quemado 24.000 hectáreas solo en Madrid (45.000 si se suma Ávila), una cantidad inmensa en una zona tan poblada como esta. Aroa Boto, de 37 años, llevaba días pensando que este momento iba a llegar, pero eso no hace más fácil dejar tu casa atrás, en manos de la suerte.

Esta monitora de natación, que ha vuelto a vivir con sus padres tras acabar una relación, vio esta mañana mucho humo por la ventana. Las pavesas volaban libres por Entrepinos, su urbanización. Le llegó un mensaje al teléfono: “Se ordena evacuar”. Estaba todavía preparando sus cosas cuando la Guardia Civil, por la calle, les metía prisa a través de un megáfono: tenían que irse cuanto antes. Aroa metió sus cosas en el coche, pero eso no era todo. Le quedaba algo más: tres perros, un cuarto de una amiga y la hija pequeña de esa amiga, que se ha quedado a su cargo porque su madre trabaja en Protección Civil y su padre es bombero forestal.

A punto de arrancar un coche que parecía el camarote de los hermanos Marx, el conserje le dijo que había que echar una mano a dos vecinos: “Uno es ciego y el otro no tiene piernas. Ah, y otra vecina mayor a la que vendría muy bien que le echaran una mano”. En 10 o 12 minutos, como mucho, todo quedó solventado. Se va a quedar en casa de otra amiga en Escalona del Alberche, un pueblo cercano coronado por un castillo medieval. Uno de sus perros es tan grande que su padre ha tenido que llevárselo con él a una finca. En algún momento deberá devolver a la niña a sus padres. Eso no le ha impedido llamar a un concejal de Villa del Prado por si necesitan ayuda allí. “Bueno, aquí nos ayudamos mucho unos a otros. Somos muy solidarios”, dice orgullosa.

La Sierra Oeste de Madrid se encuentra en una situación muy crítica desde que el miércoles, cuando comenzaron a propagarse incendios en el triángulo en el que se encuentran las provincias de Madrid, Ávila y Toledo. Las altas temperaturas y las fuertes rachas de viento los han vuelto incontrolables pese al esfuerzo de las autoridades, que cuentan incluso con ayuda internacional. Ese esfuerzo se dirigía desde un puesto de mando que también ha tenido que moverse por unas llamas que no entienden de jerarquías.

La evacuación exprés de esa zona provocó atascos en las carreteras, aunque en ningún momento se generó caos ni hubo desorganización. Si algo no ha logrado crear el incendio es pánico. Hasta un rato antes del desalojo, en Cenicientos y Cadalso de los Vidrios, por poner dos ejemplos, los bares estaban abiertos y la gente paseaba por la calle. Desde Casa Mila, un restaurante a pie de carretera en Escalona, los clientes comían paella con conejo mientras los vecinos de los pueblos de al lado huían con sus coches repletos. No es que no les importara, es que no quieren perder la calma hasta que a ellos les toca enfilar el mismo camino.

World.title: Blood on Her Tongue: A modern vampire tale not for the squeamish
World.content:
Johanna van Veen’s gothic horror Blood on Her Tongue offers up a classic vampire tale with some modern contemplations.

The book follows Lucy Goedhart as she is called to the ominously named Zwartwater (black water) estate, where her sister has taken ill. In 1887, there isn’t much in the way of medical treatment, but Lucy’s sister Sarah isn’t fighting off a regular illness.

Sarah has become obsessed with a body found in the bog of the vast estate and since interacting with the 300-year-old corpse she has become increasingly incoherent, struggles with taking care of herself and has developed an insatiable hunger.

As Lucy tries desperately to save her sister, she finds that her sister’s husband, her sister’s doctor and childhood friend, and several other characters who are present at the remote manor house all have their own interests and motivations – some as dangerous as whatever condition is plaguing Sarah.

The book is not for those easily bothered by gore. The title – Blood on Her Tongue – is a pretty good indication of what is to come. Van Veen does not shy away from the horror elements, including two separate scenes of eyeball gouging.

Like any good horror novel, the macabre monster is not the scariest part. The threats Lucy faces are from the men surrounding her sister. Her brother-in-law attempts to seduce Lucy while badgering her to send Sarah away to an asylum.

Sarah’s doctor expresses his own interest in Lucy, pushing his vision of the future while supposedly devoting himself to his patient. The mores of 19th-century upper-class society may be the biggest piece of villainy of all.

In the tradition of Dracula, Blood on Her Tongue tells its story through letters, journal entries and newspaper clippings. The personal correspondence adds to the claustrophobia of the work, with everyone limited to an isolated house, but the media reports remind the reader that the world outside does exist.

The work is the second book from Dutch author Johanna van Veen. It was published in 2025 in English and became a USA Today bestseller. Her first book, My Darling Dreadful Thing, was nominated for the Bram Stoker Award for best horror novel. Van Veen grew up in the Netherlands as a triplet, something that influenced her writing about the sisters Lucy and Sarah.

If horror is your thing, Blood on Her Tongue will creep you out and keep you turning the pages.

You can get your copy at the American Book Center.

World.title: Thousands cross finishing line as Nijmegen Vierdaagse ends
World.content:
The 108th edition of the Nijmegense Vierdaagse (four-day march) ended on Friday, with tens of thousands of walkers being welcomed with flowers by well-wishers.

British walker Simon Brownlee crossed the finishing line ahead of the rest of the walkers for the 27th time, local media reported. Brownlee, who completed the distance before 10am, told local broadcaster Omroep Gelderland that the walk “felt like home”. “I’m happy it is over and I can now relax,” he said.

Wheelchair participant Ronald van Dort was the very first person to finish, picking up his seventh medal for completing the event.

Over 45,000 walkers from 70 countries took part in this year’s series, which is proving increasingly popular among the young. Ten years ago, 7.5% of the walkers were aged 21 to 30, but this year their number rose to over 20%.

This year the event was marred by a fatal shooting just outside the area where the Vierdaagsefeesten, the street festivities accompanying the annual four-day marches, were taking place. One man has been arrested.

The shooting, and other crowd problems, led the organisers to cancel performances by urban scene artists such as Ronnie Flex and Lil’ Kleine because their presence was “attracting the wrong sort of people”, the AD reported.

World.title: Dozens of women forced into prostitution by Romanian gang
World.content:
Dozens of women may have been forced into working as prostitutes in Amsterdam’s red light district by a Romanian gang, Dutch police confirmed on Friday.

The statement follows a joint Dutch and Romanian campaign against human trafficking in the area earlier this month. Seven men were arrested during a string of raids on July 14 – four in the Netherlands and three in Romania. All were Romanian nationals.

Shortly after the arrests, police issued a video interview with one of the victims speaking Romanian, which has led more women to come forward and has resulted in other information reaching the police, the statement said.

Police now say they have spoken to several victims and say they believe more women have been trafficked. They too are said to be Romanian.

The women were lured to Amsterdam with the promise of high earnings but found themselves forced into working in brothels and handing over their earnings to the gang. They were also forced to pay “rent” for their rooms.

None of the men had jobs but were big spenders, buying expensive clothes and cars and gambling heavily, the statement said. The gang also treated part of the red light district as their “personal kingdom”.

Four men remain in custody in the Netherlands, one of whom was extradited from Romania. Another man may also be extradited soon, RTL said. They are all suspected of human trafficking and forming a criminal organisation.

According to the Parool, two of the suspects are half brothers aged 44 and 45 who have earlier convictions for trafficking in women in Romania.

More arrests have not been ruled out.

A year ago, Dutch and Romanian police arrested 13 people in a joint investigation into human trafficking and the forced prostitution of Romanian women, mainly in and around Amsterdam.

World.title: Singer Sophie Straat cleared of discrimination over mosh pit
World.content:
Discrimination hotlines in both the Netherlands and Belgium have concluded that Dutch singer Sophie Straat did not discriminate when she asked “all white men to step back” during two of her recent performances.

Last month at the Best Kept Secret festival in Beekse Bergen, Straat — real name Sophie Schwartz — asked for space for women, queer people and people of colour in the “mosh pit”, an area in front of the stage where fans dance chaotically.

She made the same request on Monday during a performance in Ghent, Belgium.

The Dutch discrimination hotline Discriminatie.nl said it received hundreds of complaints but maintains that Straat’s comments do not amount to discrimination against white men based on their colour or gender.

“The call only concerned one short, one-off mosh pit for these groups,” said the hotline. “Therefore, visitors were not refused entry to the concert.”

Belgian authorities reached the same conclusion after receiving some 200 complaints following her performance in Ghent.

“Although the statement may be perceived as polarizing or offensive, in this context it must be seen as a symbolic and artistic expression,” a spokesperson for the Belgian discrimination hotline Unia told the Flemish broadcaster VRT.

“According to the case law of the European Court of Human Rights, artistic and political expressions enjoy broad protection under freedom of expression, even when they provoke, shock or offend.”

Hate messages and death threats

Straat wrote on Instagram earlier this month that she has received “a wave of sexist, antisemitic hate messages and (death) threats, some more explicit and creative than others”.

She has also questioned where the left-wing media has been in all this, saying the public narrative is being controlled by the right.

The singer, who was raised in a Jewish home in Amsterdam’s de Pijp neighbourhood and is known for her protest songs, has said she never wanted to exclude anyone but rather wanted to make room for people who feel unsafe in a mosh pit.

World.title: Youngster arrested for participating in sadistic online network
World.content:
Police have arrested a young man from Noord Holland who they suspect of being part of the sadistic online Com network “764”.

The public prosecution department reported the arrest on Thursday, saying the suspect encouraged underage girls to cut themselves and write his online name on a wall with their own blood—so-called “bloodsigns”.

He also is said to have prompted them to write his name on their bodies with a marker, known as“fansigns”. Both are practices within the Com movement—short for The Community—for members to gain prestige.

The suspect himself, who was also charged with aggravated assault, exploitation of underage girls and possession of images of sexual child abuse, was a minor at the time of the alleged crimes. Because of that, no further details are being released.

The Com network consists of various chat groups where members recruit vulnerable young people and force them to commit acts including assault, sexual abuse and murder.

The members, from all corners of the globe, then share images of these acts online in private chat groups, using such platforms as Telegram and Discord.

According to NOS, at least 70 Dutch people are involved in this movement known as “nihilistic extremism” because the incitement to commit such extreme violence doesn’t have a clear ideological motive.

The phenomenon is especially attractive to young men.

World.title: Dangerous drivers face extra surveillance under points system
World.content:
The police and justice ministry officials are working on a system which would see traffic offenders being given points for dangerous driving – which will lead to persistent offenders coming under extra surveillance.

Motorists who have collected six points for using a mobile phone while driving or not wearing a seatbelt would come under the tougher regime, RTL Nieuws reported on Friday. No start date has yet been set.

The points will be awarded in addition to regular fines. The number of points will depend on the seriousness of the offences and speeding tickets recorded by camera will not be included.

The new system is being devised in an effort to tackle persistent offenders who do not change their behaviour despite being fined multiple times, RTL said. Last year, almost 30,000 people would have had at least six points if the new system had been in existence.

“Research shows that people who don’t stick to the rules are often responsible for accidents,” Achilles Damen from the public prosecution department told the broadcaster.

The privacy implications of monitoring specific individuals are still being assessed, RTL said.

World.title: Ajax beat Vojvodina in Conference League qualifier, Twente lose
World.content:
Ajax kicked off their European football campaign with a 4-1 win over Serbian club Vojvodina in the second qualification round of the Conference League competition in Novi Sad on Thursday evening.

The simple win sets the Amsterdammers up in a strong position ahead of the return match next week. If Ajax win again, they will meet either Irish side Shelbourne FC or Estonian club Nõmme Kalju in the third qualification round for the third-tier European competition.

The Amsterdam goal total included one for 16-year-old debutant Mohamed Abdalla, who became the youngest player to score for a Dutch club in Europe.

There was disappointment for FC Twente, who are hoping to qualify for the group stage of the Europa League. They lost 1-2 at home to Hungarian side Ferencváros and will have to pull out all the stops during the away leg next week to remain in the competition.

If they do lose, Twente will move down to the qualification rounds of the Conference League.

PSV Eindhoven and Feyenoord have qualified directly for the Champions League while NEC is taking part in the qualification competition. AZ, as winners of the KNVB Cup last season, will take part in the Europa League competition.

World.title: Unilever backs London for food division secondary listing
World.content:
Unilever’s food division, which is being sold to US sauce and spice producer McCormick, will have a secondary listing on the London stock exchange, despite an intensive lobbying campaign to list in Amsterdam.

Unilever itself has been based in London, and listed there, since 2020.

Unilever said in a statement that the secondary listing is separate to McCormick’s plans to establish an international headquarters in the Netherlands and maintain Unilever Food’s R&D facilities and operations in Wageningen.

This “reflects its commitment to the European market and the critical role the Netherlands will continue to play in the combined company”, the statement said.

Economic affairs minister Heleen Herbert said in a reaction to the sale when it was announced in March that the cabinet had already discussed developments with Unilever and would talk to the new owner “such as about a listing on the Amsterdam stock exchange”.

Unilever’s ice cream arm, spun off in 2024, is listed on the Amsterdam stock exchange as the Magnum Ice Cream Company and is headquartered in the Dutch capital.

The sale of the food arm means there is nothing left of the original Dutch part of Unilever, which was set up in 1930 through the merger of the Dutch Margarine Unie and British soap maker Lever Brothers. Unilever now focuses on personal care and household cleaning products.

World.title: Poland identifies remains of legendary anti-communist resistance fighter
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s state Institute of National Remembrance (IPN) has identified the remains of Mieczysław Dziemieszkiewicz (pictured above on the right), a prominent figure in the underground resistance that fought against the Soviet-installed communist authorities in the years after World War Two. Dziemieszkiewicz, who was killed by the communist security services in 1951 and dumped in an unmarked mass grave, was identified through a combination of historical detective work and genetic testing, including exhuming the remains of his deceased mother and sister to obtain DNA samples. “Once again, we can say that the communist authorities did not win. Heroes prevail,” declared Krzysztof Szwagrzyk, deputy head of the IPN. “Even in the most difficult situations, we must seek the truth, find those of whom no trace was supposed to remain, and restore their names.” While World War Two officially came to an end in 1945, tens of thousands of Poles, known as the “cursed soldiers” (żolnierze wyklęci), continued to fight against the Soviets and the communist regime they installed in Poland. While most had laid down arms by 1947, some continued fighting well beyond then, including Dziemieszkiewicz, who operated under the nom de guerre “Rój” (meaning “swarm”). Dziemieszkiewicz, who was 20 years old when the war ended, came from a family that had been part of Poland’s wartime resistance. His anti-communist views were hardened when his elder brother, Roman, was killed by Red Army soldiers in 1945. After being conscripted that year into the Soviet-backed Polish People’s Army, Dziemieszkiewicz defected and joined the underground resistance forces, where he rose to command a unit tasked with eliminating regime officials and members of the communist Polish Workers Party (PPR). Dziemieszkiewicz’s group killed around two dozen members of the communist security services and more than 20 informants, according to the IPN. In 1950, the communist authorities intensified efforts to dismantle Dziemieszkiewicz’s unit, using threats and blackmail to recruit hundreds of agents and informants in an effort to locate the resistance fighters. Eventually, one such informant gave up Dziemieszkiewicz’s location in exchange for a promise to release her parents from captivity. Dziemieszkiewicz found himself surrounded by several hundred soldiers and was killed while trying to escape. After his body had been identified by his family, Dziemieszkiewicz was buried in a section of Powązki Cemetery in Warsaw where the remains of those killed by the communist security services were placed en masse in unmarked graves. Exhumations by the IPN, which was established after the fall of communism to investigate communist and Nazi crimes in Poland, have located over 200 complete bodies at that site as well as several thousand bone fragments. During that work, one set of remains was found buried with an eagle symbol and remnants of a black cloth. IPN researchers realised that the item was similar to a beret that appeared in posthumous photographs of Dziemieszkiewicz’s body taken by the communist security services. That prompted them to carry out genetic testing on the remains and compare them to samples taken from Dziemieszkiewicz’s mother and sister, who were buried in a cemetery in the town of Maków Mazowiecki. “We have found ‘Rój’, commander of one of the longest-fighting units of the independence underground,” declared the IPN on Friday, announcing the confirmation of his identity. They described Dziemieszkiewicz as “legend in life and a symbol of the fight against communist oppression”. The identification was announced today during a press conference at @PrzystanekH. The identification is the result of many years of work carried out by the IPN. It was preceded by extensive archival and investigative research, the analysis of forensic evidence, archaeological… https://t.co/Rcf4wemJFc pic.twitter.com/XgMUAgSQc6 — Institute of National Remembrance (@ipngovpl_eng) July 24, 2026 At a conference announcing the findings, the IPN noted that Dziemieszkiewicz’s remains had been located right next to those of another prominent anti-communist resistance fighter, Zygmunt Szendzielarz, who fought under the nom de guerre “Łupaszko”. “It is an incredible situation that two great and distinguished soldiers of the Polish underground lie next to each other in this part of the Powązki Cemetery,” said Szwagrzyk. However, Szendzielarz, who was executed by the communist authorities in 1951, has a contested legacy, given evidence that his unit was involved in the massacre of dozens of Lithuanian civilians. Some other “cursed soldiers” have faced similar accusations of war crimes. While it was often IPN historians who uncovered evidence of such actions, the institution has more recently begun to honour those figures, particularly under the rule of the national-conservative Law and Justice government between 2015 and 2023. Opposition MPs walked out of parliament yesterday as the chamber commemorated an underground officer who fought against Nazi-German occupation and the imposition of communism in Poland, but has also been accused of a war crime against civilians https://t.co/MIY7krOxTw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 9, 2022 Dziemieszkiewicz himself, however, like most of the cursed soldiers, has not faced such accusations. In 2007, President Lech Kaczński posthumously awarded Dziemieszkiewicz the Commander’s Cross with Star of the Order of Polonia Restituta, one of Poland’s highest honours. In 2020, his image was featured on a commemorative silver coin issued by the National Bank of Poland. Through a combination of brutal repression and offering amnesties, the communist authorities managed to end most resistance efforts by 1947. However, the last “cursed soldier” to die in combat, Józef Franczak, was killed in 1963, 18 years after the end of the war.
